The Federal College of Freshwater Fisheries Technology, New Bussa, Niger State, was established in January 1978 as Federal Freshwater Fisheries School under the aegis of Kainji Lake Research Institute (KLRI), initially located at temporary site in Shagunu. Following reorganization of research institutes nationwide in 1987, when Kainji Lake Research Institute (a multi-disciplinary research institute) became a single commodity (Fisheries) Institute under the National Institute for Freshwater Fisheries Research (NIFFR), the college's name changed from Federal Freshwater Fisheries School to Federal College of Freshwater Fisheries Technology in line with similar agricultural sector colleges. The college became self-accounting from January 1989, enabling direct project funding and addressing NBTE deficiencies before accreditation visits. Located in New Bussa, Niger State, the college operates under National Institute for Freshwater Fisheries Research (NIFFR) supervision and is accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), having been granted approval to mount Pre-ND (2008), ND (2010), and HND (2013) programmes in Fisheries Technology. The college's core mandate is to train junior, intermediate and senior fisheries personnel for inland fisheries development through short and long term formal education, and to train and retrain middle-level manpower in aquaculture technology. Specific functions include: (a) to train junior, intermediate and senior fisheries personnel for inland fisheries development through short and long term formal education; (b) to train and retrain middle-level manpower in aquaculture technology; (c) to encourage women participation in fisheries through post-harvest technology training; (d) to train food technicians, technologists and chemical analysts in preservation, processing, packaging, storage and marketing of food commodities and equipment; (e) to train agricultural extension technicians to carry out extension work among rural farmers and fisher folks; (f) to organize agricultural cooperatives and exhibitions, marketing of farm produce, tools, equipment and assisting in agricultural management research; (g) to train agricultural technicians capable of applying modern farming techniques in direct agricultural production; (h) to train caterers capable of producing acceptable local and continental dishes; and (i) to be role model for fisheries, agricultural and allied tertiary institutions developing highly intellectual, skilled, creative and self-employable individuals through modern scientific, technological, research and development methods for socio-economic and political growth toward national development goals.

mda_name: 122. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF HORTICULTURE, DADIN-KOWA, GOMBE
mandate_description: The Federal College of Horticultural Technology, Dadin Kowa, is a government-owned tertiary institution located at Dadin Kowa, Yamaltu Deba Local Government Area of Gombe State, Nigeria. Approved and established with effect from April 19, 2002, by President Chief Olusegun Obasanjo's administration, the college became the first of its kind in Sub-Saharan Africa. The college is covered by Decree 35 of June 1975 on establishment of Agricultural Research Institutes and conduct of training. Operating as a research institution under the Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria (ARCN) supervised by Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, the college is accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) to award National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) certificates. The college's core mandate is to train and improve manpower in Horticultural and Landscaping Technology. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in horticulture through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes approved by NBTE; (b) to train technicians and technologists in general horticulture, floriculture, vegetable production, orchard establishment and management; (c) to provide education in agroforestry practices related to horticultural systems; (d) to train personnel in horticulture management technology; (e) to provide training in agriculture extension management for horticultural enterprises; (f) to educate students in cooperative economic management for horticultural marketing; (g) to train personnel in science laboratory technology supporting horticultural research; (h) to provide training in fishery technology and animal health and production technology; (i) to offer certificate programmes in general horticulture, floriculture, vegetable production, orchard establishment and agroforestry (1-year duration); (j) to conduct training and empowerment of youth and women in mango, guava and fruit production; (k) to provide training in orchard establishment and management; (l) to offer capacity building in modern farming technology and post-harvest handling techniques; (m) to conduct research in horticultural sciences; and (n) to empower students for labour market and self-employment. As of 2017, the institution trained 1,500 youths from 36 states in agriculture and plant production, having graduated over 1,354 students.

mda_name: 123. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF LAND RESOURCES TECHNOLOGY - OWERRI
mandate_description: The Federal College of Land Resources Technology, Owerri (FECOLART), was approved by Federal Government in the 1981-1985 4th National Development Plan to address threats of environmental degradation arising principally from soil erosion and flooding in Nigeria. Established in 1980 to train junior and intermediate personnel to participate in checking ubiquitous land degradation problems and ensuring sustainable agricultural production while conserving soil, the college is located at KM4 Old Orlu Road, Egbeada, Owerri, Imo State (temporary site formerly occupied by Conservation Centre for Eastern Zone). Academic activities commenced January 20, 1992, following recommendations of ministerial task force to address initial administrative bottlenecks. The college acquired 100 square hectares at Oforola and Obosima for permanent site, gazetted by Imo State Government in 1998. Operating as a pace-setter institution organized along collegiate system, the college introduced cognate disciplines under supervision of Director, Federal Department of Agricultural Land Resources, Abuja. However, transfer to FEPA/Federal Ministry of Water Resources & Natural Resources in May 1998 created conflict of ownership constituting major setback for infrastructural development. The college's core mandate is to train and develop skilled middle-level manpower in Land Resources Conservation and Environmental Management to reposition agriculture. Specific functions include: (a) to train middle-level manpower in land resources technology, soil conservation and environmental management through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes; (b) to develop and organize short duration courses for relevant serving professionals and private organizations to keep them abreast of modern techniques in land resources management and conservation; (c) to carry out soil advisory services for government and private agencies; (d) to provide education in soil management, soil survey and land evaluation; (e) to train personnel in erosion control, watershed management and land reclamation; (f) to educate students in irrigation and drainage engineering technology; (g) to provide training in agricultural engineering technology for land development; (h) to train personnel in environmental impact assessment and environmental monitoring; (i) to conduct applied research in land degradation control and sustainable land management; (j) to provide consultancy services to individuals, communities, local and state governments in catchment area; and (k) to award National Diploma and Higher National Diploma certificates approved by National Board for Technical Education.

mda_name: 124. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF LAND RESOURCES TECHNOLOGY, KURU - JOS
mandate_description: The Federal College of Land Resources Technology, Kuru, Jos, is a federal tertiary institution established to provide specialized education and training in land resources management, soil conservation, and environmental management for the North-Central geo-political zone and Plateau State region. Located in Kuru, near Jos, Plateau State, the college operates under Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development supervision through the Department of Agricultural Land Resources. The college was established following Federal Government recognition of environmental degradation threats arising from soil erosion, gully formation, and land degradation particularly affecting highland and plateau ecosystems requiring specialized trained manpower for sustainable agricultural production and soil conservation. The college's core mandate is to train skilled middle-level manpower in Land Resources Technology, soil conservation and environmental management specifically adapted to plateau, highland and Middle Belt ecosystems. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in land resources technology through National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes accredited by National Board for Technical Education; (b) to train technicians and technologists in soil management, soil survey, land evaluation and classification appropriate for highland zones; (c) to provide education in erosion control, gully reclamation and watershed management for plateau ecosystems; (d) to train personnel in soil conservation practices, terracing, contour farming and soil erosion prevention in highland agriculture; (e) to educate students in irrigation and drainage engineering for plateau agricultural systems; (f) to provide training in land reclamation, mine site rehabilitation and degraded land restoration; (g) to train personnel in agricultural engineering technology for land development and farm mechanization; (h) to educate students in environmental management, environmental impact assessment and monitoring; (i) to provide training in geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sensing for land resources assessment; (j) to develop and organize short-duration courses for professionals and private organizations in modern land resources management techniques; (k) to carry out soil advisory services, soil testing and land capability assessment for government agencies, farmers and private entities; (l) to conduct applied research in land degradation control, sustainable land management and environmental conservation; (m) to provide consultancy services in land resources planning and soil conservation to communities and government; and (n) to train manpower capable of repositioning agriculture through sound land management practices.

mda_name: 125. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF PRODUCE INSPECTION AND STORED PRODUCTS TECHNOLOGY, KANO
mandate_description: The Federal College of Produce Inspection and Stored Products Technology, Kano, is a specialized federal tertiary institution established to provide training in agricultural produce inspection, quality control, grading, standardization and stored products technology. Located in Kano, Nigeria's major agricultural trading hub and commercial center for northern Nigeria, the college operates under Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development through the Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria (ARCN). The college was established to address critical national need for trained inspectors, graders and technologists capable of ensuring quality standards for agricultural produce intended for export, domestic consumption and storage, particularly given Kano's strategic position as groundnut pyramid capital and major agricultural commodity trading center. Accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), the college awards National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) certificates. The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in produce inspection, quality assurance, grading, standardization and stored products technology for agricultural commodities. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in produce inspection and stored products technology through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes; (b) to train technicians and technologists in agricultural commodity grading, classification and standardization based on international and national quality standards; (c) to provide education in produce inspection techniques, sampling methods and quality assessment for grains, legumes, oilseeds and export crops; (d) to train personnel in stored products protection, pest management in storage, fumigation techniques and post-harvest loss prevention; (e) to educate students in warehouse management, storage facilities design and stored grain ecosystem management; (f) to provide training in commodity quality assurance, chemical analysis of agricultural products and food safety testing; (g) to train personnel in export produce inspection, certification and compliance with international phytosanitary standards; (h) to educate students in agricultural produce marketing, commodity trading and market information systems; (i) to provide training in post-harvest handling, drying, cleaning, packaging and preservation of agricultural commodities; (j) to train technologists in integrated pest management for stored products, biological control and safe pesticide application; (k) to educate students in food processing technology and value addition for agricultural commodities; (l) to conduct research in stored products protection, post-harvest technology and quality improvement; (m) to provide consultancy and testing services for agricultural commodity quality assessment; and (n) to train personnel supporting agricultural export development and domestic food security through proper produce handling and storage.

mda_name: 126. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF VETERINARY AND MEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNOLOGY, VOM, PLATEAU STATE
mandate_description: The Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology (also known as Federal College of Veterinary and Medical Laboratory Technology), Vom, is one of Federal Colleges of Agriculture located within National Veterinary Research Institute (NVRI), Vom, Jos South LGA, Plateau State, at altitude of 1,285 meters above sea level. The college was established in 1941 as Veterinary School, Vom, with ten students, becoming first Higher Institution in West Africa to produce graduate Veterinary Surgeons before University of Ibadan was established in 1948. Initially offering Veterinary Assistants (junior course, senior course) and Veterinary Officers training, the school discontinued Veterinary Officers' course in June 1950 when University College Ibadan assumed higher veterinary training, concentrating thereafter on 2-year Veterinary Assistants' Course. In March 1980, Veterinary School was formally accorded college status and renamed College of Animal Health and Husbandry with mandate to award Ordinary and Higher Diplomas. National Science and Technology Amendment Decree No. 46 of December 30, 1990, gave legal backing to Research Institute to conduct training for technicians and technologists for award of National Diploma (ND), Higher National Diploma (HND) and Certificates. NBTE granted accreditation for ND programmes in Animal Health and Production in 1989 and HND programmes in 1992, with college renamed Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology in 1991. In 2014, department of Veterinary Science Laboratory Technology (VSLT) was established with options in Veterinary Microbiology, Pathology, Radiology and Anaesthesiology, graduating and inducting 162 maiden graduands of Veterinary Laboratory Technology and Animal Health Technology into Veterinary Council of Nigeria (VCN) as professional para-veterinarians in 2021. The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in Animal Health, Animal Production, Livestock Extension/Management Services, Veterinary Laboratory Technology and Vocational Training who can effectively utilize training to establish and manage livestock farms. Specific functions include: (a) to provide Preliminary National Diploma in Science and Technology (1 year); (b) to offer National Diploma (ND) in Animal Health and Production Technology (2 years); (c) to provide Higher National Diploma (HND) in Animal Health (2 years) with veterinary laboratory technology specialization; (d) to offer Higher National Diploma (HND) in Animal Production (2 years); (e) to provide Higher National Diploma (HND) in Veterinary Science Laboratory Technology with options in Veterinary Microbiology, Pathology, Radiology and Anaesthesiology; (f) to train extension staff capable of bringing agro-veterinary research and innovations to livestock farmers and feeding back farmers' problems to authorities; (g) to produce men and women knowledgeable in animal production who can establish and manage livestock farms to maximum advantage; (h) to train para-veterinarians and veterinary laboratory technologists; (i) to offer degree programmes in Agricultural Science (Animal Production) through affiliation with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi; (j) to provide Post Graduate Diploma in Animal Health and Production; (k) to offer short courses in animal health, poultry production, beef and dairy production, small ruminants production, and agro-forestry; (l) to produce job-providers not job-seekers; and (m) to award certificates preparing graduates for induction into Veterinary Council of Nigeria and National Youth Service Corps mobilization.

mda_name: 127. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT - NEW BUSSA
mandate_description: The Federal College of Wildlife Management, New Bussa, is a specialized federal tertiary institution established in 1989 and located in New Bussa, Niger State, along Awuru Road, Kainji-Mokwa Expressway. Operating under the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) supervised by Federal Ministry of Environment, the college is accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) to offer National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes in wildlife management, conservation and ecotourism. Located near Kainji Lake and Kainji Lake National Park, the college benefits from proximity to Nigeria's premier wildlife conservation areas and National Institute for Freshwater Fisheries Research, providing unique opportunities for practical wildlife management training. The college's core mandate is to provide specialized education and training in wildlife management and conservation, producing middle-level manpower capable of managing Nigeria's wildlife resources sustainably. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in wildlife management through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes; (b) to train technicians and technologists in wildlife biology, ecology and behavior for effective species management; (c) to provide education in habitat management, restoration techniques and conservation biology; (d) to train personnel in wildlife monitoring, census techniques, population assessment and research methodologies; (e) to educate students in captive animal care, zoo management and ex-situ conservation; (f) to provide training in protected area management, national park administration and wildlife reserve operations; (g) to train personnel in wildlife law enforcement, anti-poaching strategies and community conservation; (h) to educate students in ecotourism development, interpretation and visitor management; (i) to provide training in human-wildlife conflict management and mitigation strategies; (j) to train technologists in wildlife health management, disease surveillance and veterinary care for wild animals; (k) to educate students in biodiversity conservation, endangered species management and recovery programmes; (l) to provide training in community-based wildlife management, participatory conservation and stakeholder engagement; (m) to train personnel in environmental education, conservation awareness and public outreach; (n) to conduct research in wildlife management, conservation biology and ecosystem management; (o) to collaborate with local communities, government agencies, non-governmental organizations and stakeholders to promote wildlife conservation and sustainable development; and (p) to ensure better education for better forest and wildlife conservation.

mda_name: 128. FEDERAL COMPETITION AND CONSUMER PROTECTION TRIBUNAL
mandate_description: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Tribunal (FCCPT or CCPT) was established by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018 (FCCPA), which commenced January 30, 2019, repealing the Consumer Protection Act CAP C25, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004. The FCCPA established two institutions for enforcement: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) and the Competition and Consumer Protection Tribunal (CCPT). The Tribunal is composed of a Chairman (must be lawyer with 10 years post-qualification experience in competition law, consumer protection law, commercial and industrial law) and six other members with 10 years professional experience in competition and consumer protection law, commerce and industry, public affairs, economics, finance, or business administration, appointed by President subject to Senate confirmation. Members serve five-year tenure from confirmation date or until attaining seventy years, whichever comes first. The Tribunal's core mandate is to adjudicate and exercise jurisdiction, powers and authority conferred by the FCCPA throughout Nigeria for promotion of competition and consumer protection. Specific functions and powers include: (a) to hear and determine appeals or review decisions of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission throughout the Federation; (b) to adjudicate on matters arising from implementation of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018; (c) to hear appeals or review decisions of sector-specific authorities after such appeals have first been heard and determined by the Commission; (d) to exercise jurisdiction over all matters relating to competition and consumer protection as conferred by FCCPA; (e) to impose penalties including administrative penalties, fines and sanctions for violations of competition and consumer protection provisions; (f) to order sale of assets where necessary to remedy anti-competitive conduct; (g) to grant injunctions, make cease and desist orders, and issue other equitable remedies; (h) to review and approve or reject Commission decisions on mergers, acquisitions, monopoly investigations and restrictive agreements; (i) to hear complaints directly filed before it by affected parties; (j) to consider matters referred to it by the Commission; (k) to enforce consumer protection rights and remedies; (l) to adjudicate disputes involving anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, monopoly situations, misleading and deceptive practices, unfair business practices, merger approvals and price regulations; (m) to make procedural rules governing its operations; (n) to maintain public records and make decisions publicly accessible; and (o) to register its decisions at Federal High Court for enforcement purposes. Appeals from Tribunal decisions go to Court of Appeal within 30 days. Under Section 104 FCCPA, the Act's provisions override all other laws (subject to Constitution) in matters relating to competition and consumer protection, establishing Tribunal's precedence in such matters.

The Federal Fire Service (FFS) was established by an Act of Parliament in April 1963, tracing origins to 1901 when Fire Service in Nigeria was established as arm of Lagos Police Fire Brigade. Operating under Fire Service Act (CAP F17 LFN 2004), the Federal Fire Service is under supervision of Ministry of Interior through Civil Defence, Fire, Immigration and Prisons Services Board (CDFIPB) established by Decree No.14 of July 1986. The Federal Government reform of Fire Services in 2007 significantly redefined the Service's mandate beyond traditional firefighting to include regulatory and policy functions. The Federal Fire Service consists of Federal Fire Commissioner (responsible for efficient administration and government of the Service under Minister's general orders and directions) and such other officers and firemen of various ranks appointed by Federal Civil Service Commission. Headquarters located at Mohammadu Buhari Way, Area 10, Garki, Abuja, with twelve zonal commands distributed nationwide. The Fire Service's core mandate encompasses firefighting, fire prevention, rescue operations and regulatory oversight of fire services nationally. Under 2007 reform, specific functions include: (a) to extinguish, control and prevent fire for saving and protection of life and property; (b) to perform humanitarian and rescue works as required under Minister's authority; (c) to regulate State and Private Fire Services throughout Nigeria; (d) to prescribe and monitor standards for promotion of fire education, fire prevention, fire safety, mitigation and investigation; (e) to ensure effective discharge of functions by State Fire Services; (f) to provide policy direction for the Nation's Fire Services; (g) to ensure standardization of fire and rescue equipment manufactured or imported into Nigeria; (h) to encourage establishment by State Fire Services of adequate number of fire stations and fire posts; (i) to establish National Fire Academy and other training facilities for training firefighters within Nigeria and African sub-region; (j) to formulate and develop training curricula and requirements for fire fighters; (k) to provide paramedical and information services during emergencies; (l) to conduct topography of allotted areas and jurisdictions; (m) to effect rescues during fire incidents, accidents and disasters; (n) to collect and collate fire statistics for planning, research and policy formulation; (o) to inspect and ensure fire safety compliance in public buildings and facilities; (p) to provide fire safety education and public enlightenment programmes; (q) to ensure preparedness and impact reduction during emergencies through adequate planning; (r) to maintain Fire Service Reward Fund; (s) to charge fees for services other than extinguishing fires at prescribed rates; (t) to coordinate national emergency responses; and (u) to make fire-fighting and fire prevention services available to non-members through training facilities. Fire Service shall not be used for suppressing civil disturbances. The Service maintains vision to produce firefighters proficient in prevention and mitigation of fire and other emergencies.

mda_name: 130. FEDERAL GOVT STAFF HOUSING LOANS BOARD
mandate_description: The Federal Government Staff Housing Loans Board is a federal government agency established to provide housing loan facilities and mortgage financing to federal civil servants and public officers to enable them acquire or construct residential accommodation. Operating under the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing (now Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development), the Board was established to address housing needs of federal government employees and facilitate home ownership among public servants. The Board's core mandate is to administer housing loan schemes for federal government staff and provide affordable financing for residential property acquisition and construction. Specific functions include: (a) to provide housing loans to eligible federal government employees for purchase or construction of residential houses; (b) to administer and manage housing loan schemes and mortgage facilities for federal civil servants; (c) to determine eligibility criteria, loan amounts, interest rates and repayment terms for housing loans; (d) to process housing loan applications from federal government staff and conduct necessary verifications; (e) to disburse approved housing loans to beneficiaries according to established procedures; (f) to monitor loan utilization and ensure funds are applied for approved housing purposes; (g) to collect loan repayments through salary deductions and other approved recovery mechanisms; (h) to maintain loan portfolio and keep accurate records of beneficiaries and loan accounts; (i) to recover outstanding loans and pursue defaulting borrowers according to established procedures; (j) to establish partnerships with mortgage banks, financial institutions and housing developers to expand financing options; (k) to promote home ownership culture among federal government employees; (l) to provide advisory services on housing matters to federal civil servants; (m) to facilitate access to affordable housing finance for public officers; (n) to collaborate with relevant housing development agencies to expand housing supply for federal workers; (o) to prepare and manage budgets for housing loan schemes; and (p) to submit periodic reports on loan portfolio, disbursements, recoveries and housing loan programme performance to supervisory ministry and relevant authorities. The Board operates to ensure that federal government employees have access to housing finance at concessionary rates, contributing to public service welfare and staff motivation while promoting the housing policy objectives of the Federal Government.

mda_name: 131. FEDERAL INSTITUTE OF INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH - OSHODI
mandate_description: The Federal Institute of Industrial Research, Oshodi (FIIRO), Lagos, is Nigeria's premier industrial research and development institute established to promote industrial and economic development through applied research, technology development and transfer. Operating under Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (formerly Federal Ministry of Science and Technology), the institute was established by Research Institutes (Establishment) Order 1977 and operates under Agricultural Research Council Decree 35 of 1975 as amended. Located in Oshodi, Lagos, Nigeria's industrial and commercial hub, FIIRO conducts research across multiple industrial sectors including food processing, chemical technology, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and engineering. The institute's core mandate is to conduct applied research, provide technical services, develop appropriate technologies, and facilitate technology transfer for industrial development. Specific functions include: (a) to conduct applied industrial research for development of technologies appropriate to Nigeria's needs and resources; (b) to provide technical and consultancy services to industries, government and private sector; (c) to develop and adapt technologies for small, medium and large-scale industries; (d) to conduct research in food processing, preservation, packaging and storage technologies; (e) to carry out research in chemical technology, pharmaceutical products, cosmetics and detergent production; (f) to conduct biotechnology research including fermentation technology, enzyme technology and industrial microbiology; (g) to provide research services in leather technology, textile processing and fiber technology; (h) to conduct research in palm oil processing, cassava processing and other agricultural commodity processing; (i) to develop appropriate technologies for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and cottage industries; (j) to provide analytical services including food analysis, chemical analysis, microbiological testing and quality assurance services; (k) to conduct pilot plant trials and demonstration of developed technologies; (l) to transfer technologies to industries through licensing, training and technical assistance; (m) to provide training programmes for industrial personnel, researchers, entrepreneurs and students; (n) to establish pilot production facilities and demonstration units for proven technologies; (o) to collaborate with universities, research institutes, industries and international organizations on research projects; (p) to commercialize research outputs and intellectual property developed by the institute; (q) to conduct feasibility studies for industrial projects and technology investments; (r) to provide equipment fabrication, maintenance and calibration services; (s) to publish research findings in journals, technical reports and conference proceedings; (t) to participate in technology exhibitions, trade fairs and industrial development programs; and (u) to advise government on industrial technology policies, standards and development strategies. FIIRO maintains modern research laboratories, pilot plants, analytical facilities and demonstration units supporting industrial research and technology development activities.

The Federal Medical Centre, Abuja, is a federal tertiary healthcare institution providing specialized medical services, training of healthcare professionals and conducting medical research. Located in Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory, the institution operates under Federal Ministry of Health as one of Nigeria's network of Federal Medical Centres established to provide tertiary healthcare services, complement teaching hospitals and ensure equitable distribution of specialized medical facilities. (m) to offer continuing professional development for healthcare workers; (n) to conduct clinical research and participate in research networks; (o) to maintain pharmacy department providing pharmaceutical services; (p) to provide physiotherapy and rehabilitation services; (q) to establish disease surveillance and infection prevention and control systems; (r) to provide public health services including health education and community outreach; (s) to maintain quality assurance and patient safety systems; and (t) to collaborate with state health authorities, teaching hospitals and other healthcare institutions.

mda_name:
51. DAVID UMAHI FEDERAL UNIVERSITY TEACHING HOSPITAL, UBURU, EBONYI STATE
**MDA Code:** 521026022
mandate_description:
DUFUTH operates as a premier healthcare institution with ultra-modern facilities, cutting-edge equipment, and innovative medical technology. The hospital's vision is to be a world-class tertiary health institution committed to effective and efficient health care delivery, qualitative training, and research. Its mission centers on an irreversible commitment to delivering world-class care with ultra-modern medical facilities, a conducive environment, and passion-driven personnel.

The hospital is mandated to provide clinical training for medical and health sciences students of DUFUHS and other affiliated institutions while rendering specialized healthcare services to patients. DUFUTH has established multiple centres of excellence including oncology, kidney transplant with dialysis centre, liver transplant facilities, and comprehensive cancer management services. The institution operates with state-of-the-art diagnostic equipment and aims to halt medical tourism abroad by providing world-class treatment within Nigeria. The hospital has activated primary healthcare centres across Ebonyi State communities including Umuka, Ugwulangwu, Ngbo, and Nwofe to extend its services to rural populations. Under the leadership of the Chief Medical Director, DUFUTH conducts free medical outreach programmes and has performed hundreds of successful surgeries in various specialized areas.

The DMO's vision is to be a public debt management institution of global reference. Its mission is to meet the government's financing needs in a prudent manner that supports economic development while proactively managing risks associated with public debt. The Office operates based on core values embodied in the principle of R-E-C-I-T-E: Respect, Excellence, Commitment, Integrity, Teamwork, and Efficiency.

The DMO's statutory functions under Sections 6 and 7 of the DMO Act 2003 include advising the Federal Government on terms and conditions of loans, restructuring, and refinancing; maintaining a complete and accurate database of all Federal Government borrowings (domestic and external) including contingent liabilities; preparing annual forecasts of debt service and borrowing capacity; efficiently managing Nigeria's domestic and external debt stocks including financial and currency risks; managing relationships with local and international creditors and investors; issuing and managing Federal Government securities; publishing debt data; and annually advising on financing gaps and borrowing requirements. The DMO has achieved significant milestones including reducing Nigeria's external debt stock, increasing external reserves, improving credit ratings, and successfully issuing Eurobonds, Sukuk bonds, and Green Bonds internationally.

The Armed Forces Act provides the legal framework for the Nigerian Armed Forces, establishing that the Armed Forces shall be charged with the defence of the Federal Republic of Nigeria by land, sea, and air and with such other duties as the National Assembly may prescribe. The President, as Commander-in-Chief, may give directives on the operational use of the Armed Forces, including for maintaining and securing public safety and public order.

The DHQ's responsibilities include deployment, sustenance, and recovery of forces deployed externally or within the country; coordinating tri-service operations; strategic planning and policy implementation; and ensuring that the Nigerian Armed Forces maintains combat readiness on land, sea, and air. The control of the Armed Forces, their joint operations, and training rest with the Chief of Defence Staff, who coordinates the three Services while the Service Chiefs are responsible for day-to-day running of their respective branches. The DHQ nurtures a professional Armed Forces that is people-centric and capable of meeting its constitutional responsibilities in a joint and collaborative environment. The DHQ conducts joint cooperation ventures and strategic seminars to optimize operational capabilities through transformation and innovation.

mda_name:
54. DEFENCE INDUSTRIES CORPORATION OF NIGERIA (DICON)
**MDA Code:** 116010001
mandate_description:
During the Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970), DICON tripled its production rates, making significant contributions to the war effort. Post-war, DICON diversified into civilian products including rural water supply equipment, industrial spare parts, and furniture. The corporation's mission is to operate ordnance factories for the manufacture and supply of arms and ammunition while using excess capacity to support local industries development. Its vision is to continuously produce and improve arms and ammunition quality to meet Nigeria's defence, security, and foreign policy needs to international standards.

In November 2023, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu signed the DICON Act 2023, which repeals previous legislation and expands the corporation's mandate. The new Act empowers DICON to operate, maintain, and control subsidiaries and ordnance factories; establish the Defence Industry Technology, Research, and Development Institute (DITRDI) for scientific and technological advancement; and foster growth of indigenous defence companies within the Military Industrial Complex. DICON has formed strategic partnerships with local and international defence firms for production of ammunition, drones, MESH systems, armoured vehicles, ballistic vests, and other defence equipment. Notable achievements include the 2019 unveiling of the Ezugwu MRAP armoured vehicle and production of medical equipment during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The DIA operates under the supervision of the Chief of Defence Staff and is headed by the Chief of Defence Intelligence (CDI), typically a major general appointed by the President. The agency's headquarters is located in Asokoro, Abuja. According to the National Security Agencies Act, the DIA's mandate encompasses protection and preservation of all military classified matters concerning Nigeria's security, both within and outside the country; responsibilities affecting defence intelligence of a military nature as determined by the President or Chief of Defence Staff; and providing strategic military intelligence to support national security objectives.

The DIA's core functions include intelligence collection through human intelligence (HUMINT), signals intelligence (SIGINT), imagery intelligence (IMINT), and open-source intelligence (OSINT); analysis and assessment to provide actionable insights for military commanders and policymakers; strategic warning and early detection of emerging security threats including terrorism, insurgency, and transnational crimes; counterintelligence operations to neutralize threats from foreign intelligence agencies and insider threats; and support to military operations including peacekeeping missions, counterinsurgency campaigns, and border security. The DIA collaborates with other intelligence agencies and international partners, and has been particularly active in providing intelligence support for operations against Boko Haram and other security threats.

mda_name:
56. DEFENCE INTELLIGENCE AGENCY CIVILIAN PENSIONS BOARD
**MDA Code:** 116012002
mandate_description:
The Board's mandate includes processing pension applications and documentation for retiring civilian staff; calculating and disbursing retirement benefits in accordance with applicable pension laws and regulations; maintaining accurate records of civilian employees' service years and contributions; liaising with the National Pension Commission and relevant pension fund administrators; addressing grievances and appeals related to pension matters; and ensuring compliance with federal pension policies within the agency. The Board works to ensure that civilian staff who have served the intelligence community receive their entitled benefits upon retirement or disengagement from service.

The establishment of a dedicated civilian pensions board recognizes the unique nature of service within intelligence agencies, where civilian staff play crucial support roles in administration, technical services, and other non-operational functions. The Board ensures these personnel are properly compensated for their years of dedicated service to national security while maintaining the confidentiality requirements inherent to intelligence work.

The objective of the relocation was to reposition the school with a focus on capacity building in support of the DIA and the Armed Forces of Nigeria through the provision of real-time defence intelligence to enhance national security. The nomenclature was changed from Defence Intelligence School to Defence Intelligence College in March 2013, thereby encapsulating the Agency's vision to make the institution a citadel of intelligence and security training in Nigeria.

The College's mandate is to provide security and intelligence training for all categories of DIA staff, personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces, and other security agencies, to enable them to perform optimally wherever they may be deployed. The vision is to develop well-trained, patriotic, and highly motivated manpower working with cutting-edge technology under effective leadership in collaboration with friendly forces, providing comprehensive and timely defence intelligence in support of national security strategy. The College offers various courses in intelligence analysis, collection techniques, counterintelligence operations, surveillance methodologies, and other specialized intelligence tradecraft to build institutional intelligence capacity across Nigeria's defence and security architecture.

The mandate of Defence Missions includes representing Nigeria's defence interests in host countries and international organizations; facilitating military-to-military cooperation and defence agreements; coordinating procurement of military equipment and technical assistance; gathering open-source military and strategic intelligence relevant to Nigeria's defence planning; supporting Nigerian military personnel on training attachments, courses, and official duties abroad; participating in international defence forums, conferences, and peacekeeping coordination; and facilitating official visits by Nigerian military officials.

Defence attachés posted to these missions serve as the primary link between the Nigerian Armed Forces and host nation militaries. They engage with defence ministries, military commands, and defence industries in their jurisdictions to advance Nigeria's military modernization objectives and strengthen international defence partnerships. The missions play important roles in Nigeria's participation in regional security arrangements under ECOWAS and the African Union, as well as cooperation with global partners through the United Nations and bilateral defence treaties.

mda_name:
59. DEFENCE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT BUREAU
**MDA Code:** 116002002
mandate_description:
The Bureau's mandate encompasses conducting and coordinating military research across various domains including weapons systems, communications technology, protective equipment, logistics, and medical research relevant to military operations; identifying emerging technologies and assessing their potential military applications; facilitating technology transfer and adaptation of foreign military technologies to Nigerian conditions; supporting the development of indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities; coordinating with DICON and other defence industries on research-driven product development; establishing partnerships with universities, polytechnics, and research institutes for defence-related research; documenting and disseminating research findings across the armed forces; and advising the defence leadership on technological developments affecting military capabilities.

The Bureau contributes to Nigeria's goal of reducing dependence on imported military equipment by fostering local research capacity and supporting the development of a domestic defence industrial base. It works within the broader framework of the Ministry of Defence's mandate to enhance the capability and sophistication of the country's defence industries.

The DSA's mandate is to promote national security and development, support military operations, and improve the Nigerian Armed Forces' cyberspace capabilities. The agency harnesses space products and services to aid the Nigerian military and other security agencies in tackling security challenges, recognizing space as a force multiplier. The DSA's vision is to create space competence capable of producing and utilizing space assets to meet the operational requirements of the Armed Forces and other security agencies.

The DSA operates through several directorates including Policy, Plans and Research; Navigation, Positioning and Timing; Communication Satellites; Launch Services and Space Operations; Earth Observation; and Cyber Security. Key achievements include the production of over 640 topographic maps supporting various security operations, identification of illegal refining sites, enhanced monitoring of military zones, and improved border security. The agency has established a Geospatial Intelligence Fusion and Data Center and works to develop Nigeria's indigenous rocket engineering capacity. The DSA provides secured satellite communication to the Armed Forces and is establishing Earth observation stations in military formations across all geopolitical zones. The agency is headed by the Chief of Defence Space Administration and operates in collaboration with the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA).

mda_name:
61. DEFENCE SPACE SCHOOL, OROGUN, DELTA STATE
**MDA Code:** 116018002
mandate_description:
The school's mandate includes providing foundational and advanced training in space science and technology applications relevant to military operations; developing technical skills in satellite communications, remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and related technologies; training personnel in the operation and maintenance of space-based systems used by the Armed Forces; conducting courses in cyber security and space domain awareness; supporting the Defence Space Administration's capacity building objectives; and preparing Nigerian defence personnel for specialized roles in space operations.

The establishment of the Defence Space School reflects Nigeria's commitment to developing indigenous capacity in the strategic space domain. The school works to ensure that the Nigerian Armed Forces have trained personnel capable of leveraging space technologies for enhanced operational effectiveness. The curriculum covers both theoretical foundations and practical applications, preparing graduates to support the DSA's mission of utilizing space assets for national security and defence operations.

mda_name:
62. DENTAL TECHNOLOGISTS REGISTRATION BOARD OF NIGERIA
**MDA Code:** 521007001
mandate_description:
The Board's statutory functions include determining what standards of knowledge and skill are to be attained by persons seeking to become members of the profession and improving those standards from time to time as circumstances may permit; securing, in accordance with the Act, the establishment and maintenance of a register of persons registered as members of the profession and the publication of lists of those persons; conducting examinations in the profession and awarding certificates or diplomas to successful candidates; prescribing fees for examinations, registration, and other services; and performing other functions conferred by the Act.

The Board maintains the register of qualified dental technologists and issues registration certificates. It establishes and reviews codes of conduct for professional practice and has established a Dental Technologists Disciplinary Committee to consider cases of professional misconduct referred by the Investigating Panel. The Board approves training institutions and their curricula, conducts accreditation visits, and determines which qualifications (domestic and foreign) are acceptable for registration purposes. The minimum qualifications accepted by the Board are specified in the Third Schedule to the Act, ensuring that only properly trained practitioners are authorized to practice dental technology in Nigeria.

mda_name:
63. DENTAL THERAPISTS REGISTRATION BOARD OF NIGERIA
**MDA Code:** 521039001
mandate_description:
The Board's statutory mandate includes determining what standards of knowledge and skill are to be attained by persons seeking to become members of the dental therapy profession and improving those standards from time to time; securing the establishment and maintenance of a register of persons registered under the Act as members of the profession and publishing lists of those persons; conducting examinations in the profession and awarding certificates or diplomas to successful candidates; prescribing fees for examinations and registration; and performing other functions conferred by the Act.

The Board's key functions include registering and issuing valid renewable licenses to Dental Therapists, Dental Surgery Technicians, and Dental Surgery Assistants; inspecting and monitoring training and practice of professionals; approving and accrediting training programmes and institutions; ensuring professionals operate within the confines of the registration act and comply with professional ethics; and eliminating quackery in dental therapy practice. The Board has established the Dental Therapists Disciplinary Committee to consider and determine cases of professional misconduct referred by the Investigating Panel. The DThRBN works to ensure Nigerians receive quality oral healthcare from properly trained and licensed practitioners while providing leadership in promoting conditions for professionals and enforcing regulations against poor oral hygiene practices.

mda_name:
64. DIRECTORATE OF STATE SECURITY SERVICE
**MDA Code:** 157002001
mandate_description:
According to the National Security Agencies Act, the State Security Service is charged with responsibility for the prevention and detection of any crime against the internal security of Nigeria; the protection and preservation of all non-military classified matters concerning the internal security of Nigeria; and such other responsibilities affecting internal security within Nigeria as the National Assembly or the President may deem necessary. The principal officer of the agency reports directly to the President of Nigeria.

The DSS operates as Nigeria's primary internal security and counterintelligence agency, conducting intelligence operations to protect the nation from domestic threats including terrorism, espionage, sabotage, and other threats to national security. The agency provides protective intelligence and security for high-ranking government officials, conducts background investigations, monitors threats to public order, and works to prevent activities that could destabilize Nigeria's constitutional government. The DSS also collaborates with other security agencies on matters of overlapping jurisdiction and participates in inter-agency security coordination. The agency has offices across all states of the federation and maintains a significant role in Nigeria's overall national security architecture.

mda_name:
65. DIRECTORATE OF TECHNICAL COOPERATION IN AFRICA
**MDA Code:** 119007001
mandate_description:
The Directorate's mandate encompasses coordinating technical assistance programmes to African countries in areas where Nigeria has developed capacity; facilitating the exchange of experts, professionals, and technical personnel between Nigeria and other African nations; managing scholarship programmes for African students to study in Nigerian institutions; organizing training programmes and workshops for participants from other African countries; coordinating Nigeria's contributions to regional and continental technical cooperation initiatives; liaising with the African Union and regional economic communities on technical cooperation matters; and documenting and evaluating the impact of Nigeria's technical cooperation programmes.

Through the Directorate, Nigeria provides technical assistance in various fields including healthcare, agriculture, education, infrastructure, public administration, and security sector development. The programmes reflect Nigeria's commitment to using its resources and expertise to support the development of fellow African nations while strengthening bilateral relationships and Nigeria's diplomatic influence on the continent. The Directorate works with Nigerian ministries, agencies, and institutions to identify areas of technical strength that can benefit other African countries.

mda_name:
66. DIVISION OF AGRICULTURAL COLLEGE, ABU ZARIA
**MDA Code:** 517022001
mandate_description:
The Division's mandate includes providing agricultural education at various levels including diploma, certificate, and short courses; conducting research in agricultural sciences relevant to Nigeria's food security and agricultural development; providing extension services to farming communities in the surrounding regions; training agricultural technicians and middle-level manpower for the agricultural sector; developing and disseminating improved agricultural practices and technologies; supporting farmer education and empowerment programmes; and collaborating with agricultural research institutes, extension agencies, and farmer organizations.

The Division contributes to ABU's broader mission in agricultural development, which includes the Faculty of Agriculture and the Institute for Agricultural Research. It plays a role in addressing Nigeria's need for trained agricultural professionals who can support farmers, agribusinesses, and agricultural development programmes. The Division's programmes are designed to produce graduates with practical skills applicable to various aspects of agricultural production, processing, and marketing, contributing to Nigeria's agricultural transformation agenda.

mda_name:
67. ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRIMES COMMISSION (EFCC)
**MDA Code:** 111009001
mandate_description:
The EFCC is mandated to investigate and prosecute all economic and financial crimes including advance fee fraud (419 fraud), money laundering, counterfeiting, illegal fund transfers, futures market fraud, fraudulent encashment of negotiable instruments, computer credit card fraud, contract scams, and other financial crimes. The Commission also enforces the provisions of various laws including the Money Laundering Act, the Failed Banks Act, the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, and relevant sections of the Criminal and Penal Codes relating to economic and financial crimes.

The EFCC's functions include investigating reports of financial crimes and prosecuting offenders; identifying, tracing, freezing, confiscating, and seizing proceeds derived from terrorist financing and related offences; adopting measures to eradicate the commission of economic and financial crimes; collaborating with government bodies within and outside Nigeria on the eradication of economic and financial crimes; examining and investigating reported cases of suspicious financial transactions; establishing and maintaining a system for identifying, collecting, analyzing, and disseminating information on economic and financial crimes. The Commission has secured numerous convictions and recovered substantial assets, though it has faced criticism regarding political influence and selective enforcement. The EFCC Academy provides training for investigative officers.

The ECN's vision is to ensure adequate, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable energy supply for the nation's economic and sociopolitical development. Its mission is to promote sustainable energy development in Nigeria through the production of strategic plans and coordination of national policies. The Commission serves as a centre for gathering and dissemination of information relating to national policy in the field of energy.

The Commission's functions include serving as the focal point for energy planning and coordination in Nigeria; promoting the development and optimal utilization of all energy resources including the introduction of new and alternative energy sources such as solar, wind, biomass, and nuclear energy; advising the Federal Government on matters relating to energy policy; coordinating energy-related research and development activities; promoting efficient energy use and conservation; developing standards and codes of practice for energy equipment; collaborating with states and local governments on energy development; establishing linkages with international energy organizations and facilitating technology transfer; and conducting energy data collection, analysis, and publication. The ECN operates through various research centres and works to achieve Nigeria's energy transition goals including tripling renewable energy and doubling energy efficiency targets.

mda_name:
69. ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH OFFICERS TUTORS, IBADAN
**MDA Code:** 521017001
mandate_description:
The centre's mandate includes providing pedagogical training to environmental health professionals preparing to become tutors and instructors; developing curriculum and teaching methodologies for environmental health education; training tutors in modern instructional techniques and educational technologies; upgrading the skills of existing environmental health tutors; conducting research in environmental health education and training methods; developing instructional materials and resources for environmental health programmes; and supporting the standardization of environmental health education across Nigeria.

The establishment of a dedicated tutors training centre reflects the importance of quality instruction in producing competent environmental health officers. Environmental health professionals play crucial roles in disease prevention, sanitation enforcement, food safety inspection, and community health promotion. By training tutors who can effectively transfer knowledge and skills, the centre contributes to the development of a competent environmental health workforce capable of addressing Nigeria's public health challenges. The centre works in coordination with the Environmental Health Officers Registration Council of Nigeria (EHORECON) to ensure training programmes meet professional standards.

mda_name:
70. ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH REGISTRATION COUNCIL OF NIGERIA (EHORECON)
**MDA Code:** 535017001
mandate_description:
The Council's statutory mandate includes determining what standards of knowledge and skill are to be attained by persons seeking to become members of the profession of Environmental Health and improving those standards as circumstances may permit; securing the establishment and maintenance of a register of persons registered under the Act as members of the profession and publishing lists of those persons; conducting examinations in the profession and awarding certificates or diplomas to successful candidates; establishing and reviewing a code of conduct for effective practice of the Environmental Health profession; and performing other functions conferred by the Act.

EHORECON's key functions include registering Environmental Health Officers, Environmental Health Technicians, and Environmental Health Assistants; issuing renewable practice licenses valid for two years; accrediting training programmes and institutions offering environmental health courses at National Diploma, Higher National Diploma, and degree levels; inspecting and monitoring professional practice; enforcing professional standards and ethics; and eliminating quackery in environmental health practice. The Council has established an Environmental Health Disciplinary Committee and Investigating Panel to handle cases of professional misconduct. EHORECON works to ensure that environmental health professionals are equipped with investigative, analytical, communicative, educative, organizational, and attitudinal skills necessary for effective practice in areas including sanitation, food hygiene, disease control, and environmental standards enforcement.

The Authority's mandate encompasses registering and regulating equipment leasing companies operating in Nigeria; establishing standards and guidelines for equipment leasing transactions; promoting the development of the equipment leasing industry as a financing alternative; protecting the interests of lessees and lessors in lease transactions; collecting and disseminating data on the equipment leasing sector; advising government on policies affecting equipment leasing; coordinating with the Central Bank of Nigeria, Securities and Exchange Commission, and other financial regulators; and promoting best practices in equipment leasing operations.

Equipment leasing plays an important role in Nigeria's economic development by facilitating access to capital equipment for businesses, particularly small and medium enterprises. The Authority works to create an enabling environment for equipment leasing, addressing issues such as legal documentation, tax treatment, registration requirements, and dispute resolution. By promoting equipment leasing, the Authority supports the acquisition of productive equipment in sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, construction, and healthcare, contributing to economic growth and employment generation.

The mission's mandate includes representing Nigeria in WTO negotiations and deliberations; monitoring developments in international trade rules and their implications for Nigeria; participating in dispute settlement proceedings affecting Nigeria's trade interests; coordinating with other developing countries on common trade positions; reporting on WTO activities and advising the Nigerian government on trade policy implications; facilitating Nigeria's compliance with WTO obligations; engaging with other international trade organizations in Geneva including UNCTAD; and supporting Nigerian businesses in understanding and leveraging WTO agreements.

Nigeria's participation in the WTO is critical for its trade relations given the organization's role in setting rules for international commerce, resolving trade disputes, and negotiating trade liberalization. The Geneva mission engages in negotiations across various WTO committees covering goods, services, intellectual property, agriculture, and development issues. The mission works to ensure that Nigeria's interests as a developing country are represented in trade rule-making, particularly on issues such as special and differential treatment, trade facilitation, agricultural subsidies, and industrial policy space. The mission also coordinates Nigeria's engagement with the WTO's Trade Policy Review Mechanism and technical assistance programmes.

mda_name:

mandate_description:
The school's mandate includes providing formal cooperative education through certificate and diploma programmes; training cooperative society officers, managers, and board members; conducting short courses and workshops on cooperative management and governance; developing curricula relevant to modern cooperative practice; conducting research on cooperative development issues; providing consultancy services to cooperative societies and government agencies; promoting cooperative principles and best practices; and supporting the government's cooperative reform and revival initiatives.

The school's programmes cover cooperative economics and management, cooperative law, accounting for cooperatives, cooperative governance, and related business disciplines. Graduates are equipped to serve in cooperative societies, government cooperative departments, agricultural organizations, and financial institutions. The school contributes to the Federal Government's agenda of reviving and reforming cooperative societies as vehicles for economic empowerment, particularly in agriculture. The Sokoto location enables the school to serve the cooperative development needs of the northern region while contributing to national cooperative education objectives.

The FCTA is headed by a Minister appointed by the President, who exercises powers delegated by the President (who acts as the Governor of the FCT). The Permanent Secretary is the Accounting Officer and Chief Administrative Officer. Seven mandate secretariats were created: Education, Transport, Agriculture and Rural Development, Health and Human Services, Social Development, Legal Services, and Area Council Services. The Federal Capital Development Authority (FCDA) oversees physical infrastructure development.

The FCTA's mandate includes building and administering the Federal Capital Territory in compliance with the Abuja Master Plan; providing governance, infrastructure, and services to FCT residents; implementing policies for urban development, housing, and land administration; managing the six area councils (Abuja Municipal, Gwagwalada, Abaji, Kuje, Bwari, and Kwali); ensuring provision of utilities, transportation, and social services; maintaining security, environmental standards, and public health; enforcing building codes and development control; and managing the transition from Lagos to Abuja as Nigeria's capital. The FCTA operates through various departments and agencies to deliver municipal services while maintaining Abuja's status as one of Africa's best-planned cities.

The Commission's statutory functions under Section 4 of the FCC Act include working out an equitable formula for the distribution of all cadres of posts in the civil and public services of the Federation and States, the armed forces, the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies, government-owned bodies corporate, and extra-ministerial departments and parastatals; promoting, monitoring, and enforcing compliance with the principles of proportional sharing of all bureaucratic, economic, media, and political posts at all levels of government; taking legal measures including prosecuting heads or staff of ministries or agencies that fail to comply with federal character principles; advising governments on redressing problems of imbalances and reducing fears of relative deprivation and marginalisation; and ensuring clear criteria and conditions for appointments are established.

The FCC monitors recruitment exercises across federal establishments to ensure equitable distribution among states and the FCT. The Commission categorizes representation into adequately represented (2.5-3%), under-represented (1.5-2.4%), grossly under-represented (under 1.5%), and over-represented (above 3%) status. The Commission's mandate extends to ensuring fairness in the distribution of socio-economic amenities and infrastructure across the federation, addressing historical inequalities, and promoting national unity through equitable access to opportunities.

The Constitution empowers the FCSC to appoint persons to offices (other than those of Permanent Secretary) in the Federal Civil Service; exercise disciplinary control over persons holding such offices; and promote and transfer such persons within the civil service. No officer can be appointed into the Civil Service without FCSC authorization if they have been convicted of a crime or had previously been dismissed or asked to resign or retire from government service.

The Commission's specific functions include representing at Senior Staff Committee meetings of Ministries; reviewing and approving recommendations on disciplinary cases of senior officers; ratifying promotions of officers to senior positions, including conducting promotion interviews and examinations; hearing appeals on matters of appointment, promotion, and discipline; ensuring compliance with appointment, promotion, and disciplinary guidelines; coordinating with the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; and maintaining standards of professionalism and meritocracy in the civil service. The FCSC plays a crucial role in ensuring that Nigeria's federal civil service operates on principles of merit, fairness, and due process, though its jurisdiction has been reduced over time as various agencies and services have been placed under separate boards.

The college's primary mandate is to train middle-level manpower for the cooperative subsector of the economy at National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) levels. Beyond its core mandate in Cooperative Economics and Management, the college has evolved into a multidisciplinary institution offering programmes in Accountancy, Business Administration, Banking and Finance, Computer Science, and Home and Rural Economics. The college also runs Agricultural Technology programmes and plans to introduce additional courses including Agribusiness Management and Agricultural Extension.

FCC Ibadan is regulated by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), which has accredited its programmes. Graduates of HND programmes are eligible for the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). The college maintains the Cooperative Innovation and Empowerment Centre to support the Federal Ministry of Agriculture's agenda to revive and reform cooperative societies in Nigeria. The institution offers short courses, workshops, and seminars for officers and board members of cooperative societies, combining formal academic programmes with practical cooperative development support. The college operates with a strike-free academic calendar and emphasizes practical-oriented education preparing students for careers in cooperatives, finance, and business.

The college was established as an in-service training institution for cooperative stakeholders and staff of government departments responsible for the supervision of cooperative societies and cooperative development. Initially, trainees were those sponsored by government and cooperative societies. The college started with courses leading to the award of Certificate in Cooperative Studies and later introduced the Diploma in Cooperative Studies to meet increasing demand for higher cooperative education.

The college's programmes have expanded significantly. The National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) accredited the National Diploma programmes with effect from the 2004/2005 Academic Session. The Higher National Diploma (HND) Programme in Cooperative Economics and Management was introduced and accredited in 2008 as a two-year (four-semester) programme. Beyond regular academic programmes, the college runs short courses, workshops, consultancy services, and seminars for officers and board members of cooperative societies and other stakeholders. The college now offers various ND and HND programmes as well as certificate courses designed for skills acquisition and vocational training. The institution aims to equip graduates with transformative educational experiences and prepare them for the labor market and entrepreneurship.

mda_name:
79. FEDERAL COOPERATIVE COLLEGE, OJI RIVER
**MDA Code:** 215031001
mandate_description:
The college was initially established as an in-service training institution for cooperative stakeholders and government department staff responsible for cooperative societies supervision and development. It started with courses leading to certificates and diplomas in cooperative studies. A significant milestone was achieved in the 1988/89 academic session when the college introduced National Diploma programmes in Cooperative Economics and Management. Currently, the college has four major departments with NBTE accreditation at both ND and HND levels: Cooperative Economics and Management, Banking and Finance, Business Administration, and Computer Science.

The college is regulated by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) and supervised by the Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria (ARCN). There are ongoing initiatives to expand programmes to include Mass Communication, Agricultural Technology, Home and Resource Economics, Hospitality and Tourism Management, and Science Laboratory Technology. The college also has plans to transform into a Federal Cooperative Polytechnic through National Assembly legislation. FCC Oji River serves as a host for national training workshops for cooperative stakeholders from the South-East and South-South zones, supporting the Federal Government's Renewed Hope Cooperative Reform and Revamp Programme. The curriculum emphasizes self-belief, self-determination, and market readiness, with mandatory practical entrepreneurship training ensuring graduates become potential business owners.

mda_name:
80. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, AKURE
**MDA Code:** 215021001
mandate_description:
The college's vision is to be a world-class agricultural training institution making direct and sustainable impacts on gainful youth employment, food security, and improved livelihoods for farmers. Its mission includes integrating available manpower and resources into agricultural sector opportunities; revolutionizing vocational training and short courses; incorporating value chain concepts and ICT into curriculum; and improving community relations through adopted schools and villages programmes.

FECA has offered both National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes since 1993 in key areas of agriculture including Agricultural Technology, Crop Production, Animal Health and Production, Agricultural and Bio-Environmental Engineering, and other related fields. The college is accredited by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) and graduates are eligible for NYSC mobilization. The college maintains crop farms (including cash crops such as cocoa, palm trees, coffee, and rubber), livestock facilities, and demonstration plots for practical training. FECA is a certified master trainer institution in Agribusiness and Value Chain Studies with international partnerships including Bern University of Applied Sciences, Switzerland, and the University of Queensland, Australia. The college regularly conducts vocational training courses, skill development workshops, and capacity-building programmes sponsored by the Federal Ministry of Agriculture for unemployed graduates, farmers, and agricultural stakeholders.

The Federal School of Survey, Oyo, Oyo State, is Nigeria's pioneer and only specialized institution for surveying and geoinformatics education. Established in 1908 as Government Departmental Training Institution attached to Colonial Survey Department in Lagos, the institution is older than Nigeria itself (named in 1914). The School moved from Lagos to Okene, then Ibadan (1926), finally settling in Oyo (1934). Became federal institution under Federal Ministry of Works and Housing in 1967. Located on 250 hectares in Oyo, the School awards National Diploma and Higher National Diploma in Surveying and Geoinformatics. As first modern surveying training institution in Nigeria and Africa, approximately 80-85% of Nigeria's registered professional surveyors are products of this institution. The Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development (formerly Ministry of Mines and Steel Development, renamed to emphasize solid minerals sector) was established in 1985 to unlock economic potentials of Nigeria's solid minerals sub-sector. The Ministry operates under Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act 2007 which repealed Minerals and Mining Act 1999, vesting all property in and control of mineral resources in Federal Government. Led by Minister of Solid Minerals Development (current: Dr. Oladele Henry Alake), the Ministry implements National Minerals and Metals Policy and Roadmap for Growth and Development of Nigerian Mining Industry (2016). The Ministry manages Mining Cadastre Office (MCO) as independent agency for mineral titles administration.

**Core Mandate:** To exploit Nigeria's mineral endowments in environmentally sustainable manner and establish vibrant minerals and metals industry for wealth creation, poverty reduction, economic growth and GDP contribution.

**Statutory Functions:**

(e) Maintain Mining Cadastre cadastral maps and records of mineral title locations and ownership
(f) Conduct geological surveys through Nigerian Geological Survey Agency identifying mineral deposits
(g) Operate Mines Inspectorate Department inspecting mining operations for safety and standards compliance
(h) Enforce environmental compliance through Mines Environmental Compliance Department
(i) Regulate artisanal and small-scale mining operations
(j) Promote investment in mining sector and attract foreign direct investment
(k) Manage Solid Minerals Development Fund for sector financing
(l) Develop mining infrastructure and mineral processing facilities
(m) Regulate exploitation of gold, coal, bitumen, limestone, iron ore, lead-zinc, barites and other minerals
(n) Ensure sustainable mining practices and environmental protection
(o) Coordinate Federal Mines Offices in all 36 states and FCT
(p) Promote local content and value addition in mining sector
(q) Combat illegal mining and mineral smuggling
(r) Facilitate technology transfer and mining skills development
(s) Maintain mineral title database and geo-mining information systems
(t) Ensure mining sector contribution to GDP and economic diversification
