mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs handles specialized government functions not assigned to other ministries and coordinates relationships between federal government and state/local governments. The Ministry emerged from various restructurings to address cross-cutting issues requiring dedicated ministerial attention. Led by Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, the Ministry coordinates matters requiring inter-governmental cooperation, special interventions, and liaison functions across tiers of government under Nigeria's federal system.

**Core Mandate:** To handle special duties assigned by President, coordinate inter-governmental affairs, facilitate federal-state-local government cooperation, and manage special intervention programmes.

The Federal Ministry of Transport is responsible for formulating and implementing policies for all transport modes including road transport, rail transport, maritime transport, aviation, and inland waterways. Following President Tinubu's 2023 cabinet restructuring, aviation and maritime functions were separated into dedicated ministries (Aviation and Aerospace Development; Marine and Blue Economy), with Transport Ministry now focusing primarily on road transport, rail transport and transport policy coordination. mda_name: 185. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (renamed from Federal Ministry of Water Resources in October 2024 to emphasize sanitation mandate) is responsible for water resources development, water supply, irrigation, flood control, dam construction and sanitation. The Ministry manages 240 dams and 14 River Basin Development Authorities covering Nigeria's major river systems. Following cabinet reshuffle, sanitation functions previously under environment or health were consolidated with water resources recognizing linkage between water supply and sanitation (WASH sector).

mandate_description:

Established to address gender disparities and promote women's advancement in Nigeria, the Ministry coordinates National Gender Policy implementation, combats gender-based violence, promotes women's economic empowerment and ensures gender mainstreaming across all sectors. The Federal College of Education (Technical) Isu, Ebonyi State, is one of six Federal Colleges of Education established by the Federal Government in May 2020 under President Muhammadu Buhari's administration, distributed across Nigeria's six geo-political zones to address teacher shortages. mda_name: 102. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF EDUCATION IWO, OSUN STATE
mandate_description: The Federal College of Education Iwo, Osun State, is one of six Federal Colleges of Education established on November 18, 2019, by President Muhammadu Buhari's administration, representing the South-West geo-political zone's allocation. Located in Iwo, Osun State, the college operates under the Federal Colleges of Education Act CAP F8 LFN 2004. The institution was established to address critical shortage of qualified teachers needed for Universal Basic Education (UBE) delivery. The college's statutory mandate is to provide full-time courses of teaching, instruction and training in technology, applied science, commerce, arts, social sciences, humanities and management, and to carry out research in the development and adaptation of educational techniques. Specific functions include: (a) to produce well-qualified teachers holding the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) to teach in primary and junior secondary schools; (b) to establish and maintain teaching units within the college or extramural departments as may be determined by the Council; (c) to institute and award fellowships, medals, prizes and other academic distinctions; (d) to mount exhibitions and displays designed to foster appreciation of educational trends, scope and requirements; (e) to erect, provide, equip and maintain educational, recreational and residential facilities for students and staff; (f) to conduct research in development and adaptation of teaching techniques and methodologies; and (g) to perform any other acts whether incidental to the foregoing powers that may advance the college's objectives. mda_name: 103. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF EDUCATION JAMA'ARE, BAUCHI STATE
mandate_description: The Federal College of Education Jama'are, Bauchi State, is one of six Federal Colleges of Education established in May 2020 by President Muhammadu Buhari's administration, representing the North-East geo-political zone's allocation. Located in Jama'are, Bauchi State, the college operates under the Federal Colleges of Education Act CAP F8 LFN 2004. The establishment was driven by Federal Government recognition that Bauchi, Benue, Ebonyi, Osun, Sokoto and Edo states lacked Federal Colleges of Education, representing deliberate policy intervention to address geographical imbalances and enhance teacher production capacity for Universal Basic Education implementation. The college's statutory mandate is to provide full-time courses of teaching, instruction, and training in technology, applied science, commerce, arts, social sciences, humanities and management. Specific functions include: (a) to produce qualified teachers holding the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) capable of teaching in primary and junior secondary schools nationwide; (b) to carry out research in development and adaptation of educational techniques and methodologies; (c) to establish and maintain teaching units, schools, or extramural departments within the college as the Governing Council may determine; (d) to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, medals, prizes and other academic titles and distinctions; (e) to mount exhibitions and displays designed to foster appreciation of educational trends, scope and requirements; (f) to erect, provide, equip and maintain educational, recreational and residential facilities for staff and students; and (g) to perform other acts whether incidental or not that may advance the college's educational objectives as specified in the Act.

The Federal College of Education Katsina, formerly Federal Advanced Teachers' College Katsina, was founded in 1976 as one of Nigeria's pioneering teacher training institutions. The Federal College of Education Obudu is a federal tertiary institution located in Obudu, Cross River State, Nigeria, established under the Federal Colleges of Education Act CAP F8 LFN 2004. The Federal College of Education (Special), Oyo, was established on October 5, 1977, as Federal Advanced Teachers College (Special) and is the only specialized college of its kind in Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa dedicated to special education. mda_name: 114. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF FISHERIES AND MARINE TECHNOLOGY - LAGOS
mandate_description: The Federal College of Fisheries and Marine Technology, Lagos, assumed its present status as a full-fledged technological institution in 1992, having been established in 1969 as Federal School of Fisheries. Located at 2 Wilmot Point Road, Bar Beach, Victoria Island, Lagos, the college operates as a monotechnic approved by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE). The transformation from vocational training institute to composite College of Technology resulted from comprehensive re-examination of training scope necessitated by phenomenal growth of Nigeria's fisheries and maritime sector requiring higher level indigenous expertise. The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in areas of Fisheries Technology (freshwater, brackish and marine), including aquaculture, fish processing, fishing gear design and construction, and to train deep-sea fishermen to handle dermasal and pelagic ships, alongside interwoven training of maritime professionals (traditional seafarers and shore managers) supporting national and international maritime trade based on International Maritime Organisation (IMO) Safer Shipping and Cleaner Ocean principles. Specific functions include: (a) to provide tertiary-level training in Fisheries Technology, Marine Engineering and Nautical Science through National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes; (b) to train fisheries technicians and technologists in freshwater, brackish water and marine fisheries; (c) to provide aquaculture technology training including fish farming and hatchery management; (d) to train personnel in fish processing, preservation, packaging and storage; (e) to provide fishing gear design, construction and maintenance training; (f) to train deep-sea fishermen for dermasal and pelagic fishing operations; (g) to provide Maritime Transport and Business Management education; (h) to train marine engineers and nautical science professionals; (i) to train industrial and labour relations personnel for maritime sector; (j) to conduct research in fisheries and marine technology; and (k) to provide consultancy services in fisheries and maritime fields. Supervised by Federal Ministry of Agriculture through Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria (ARCN), the college has benefited from institutional support from FAO and JICA, with graduates dominating shipping and industrial fishing sub-sectors.

mda_name: 115. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF FOREST RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, EBONYI STATE (SOUTH-EAST)
mandate_description: The Federal College of Forest Resources Management, Ishiagu, Ebonyi State, is a federal tertiary institution established to provide specialized education and training in forestry and environmental management, representing the South-East geo-political zone. Located in Ishiagu, Ebonyi State, the college operates under the auspices of Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) supervised by Federal Ministry of Environment and is fully accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) to train middle-level manpower in forestry and environmental related disciplines. The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in forestry and environmental related disciplines for sustenance and development of forestry and agriculture in Nigeria. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in forestry technology through National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes; (b) to train forestry technicians and technologists in sustainable forest management; (c) to provide education and training in environmental management and conservation; (d) to train personnel in forest resource assessment, inventory and monitoring; (e) to provide training in agroforestry, forest plantation establishment and management; (f) to educate students in wildlife management and biodiversity conservation within forest ecosystems; (g) to train personnel in wood science, forest products technology and timber utilization; (h) to provide training in forest nursery management and tree breeding; (i) to educate students in forest protection, pest management and fire control; (j) to train personnel in community forestry, participatory forest management and extension services; (k) to conduct applied research in forestry and environmental management; (l) to provide awareness on climate change mitigation through tree planting and forest conservation; and (m) to award certificates preparing graduates for National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) mobilization. During World Environment Day 2022, Acting Provost Dr. Mrs. Emeghara Ukamaka Ursulla emphasized the college's role in training professionals for sustainable environmental management and highlighting adverse effects of climate change.

mda_name: 116. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF FOREST RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, MAIDUGURI, BORNO STATE (NORTH-EAST)
mandate_description: The Federal College of Forest Resources Management, Maiduguri, Borno State, is a federal tertiary institution established to provide specialized education and training in forestry and environmental management, representing the North-East geo-political zone. Located in Maiduguri, Borno State, the college operates under the auspices of Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) supervised by Federal Ministry of Environment and is fully accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE). The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in forestry and environmental related disciplines for sustenance and development of forestry and agriculture in Nigeria, with particular focus on savannah and Sahel ecosystem management relevant to the North-East region. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in forestry technology through National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes; (b) to train forestry technicians and technologists in sustainable forest and woodland management appropriate for savannah ecosystems; (c) to provide education and training in environmental management, desertification control and land degradation prevention; (d) to train personnel in dryland forest resource assessment, inventory and monitoring; (e) to provide training in agroforestry systems suitable for semi-arid zones, shelterbelt establishment and management; (f) to educate students in wildlife management and biodiversity conservation in savannah and Sahel ecosystems; (g) to train personnel in wood science, non-timber forest products and gum arabic production; (h) to provide training in tree nursery management, seed technology and species selection for arid zones; (i) to educate students in rangeland management, pasture improvement and fodder production; (j) to train personnel in community-based natural resource management and extension services in rural areas; (k) to conduct applied research in forestry, environmental management and climate change adaptation for dryland ecosystems; (l) to provide training in watershed management, soil conservation and environmental restoration; and (m) to award certificates preparing graduates for National Youth Service Corps mobilization and employment in forestry, agriculture and environmental sectors.

mda_name: 117. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF FOREST RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, SAKPOBA, EDO STATE (SOUTH-SOUTH)
mandate_description: The Federal College of Forest Resources Management, Fugar (Sakpoba), Edo State, is a federal tertiary institution located in Fugar, Edo State, representing the South-South geo-political zone's forestry education infrastructure. Operating under the auspices of Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) supervised by Federal Ministry of Environment and fully accredited by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), the college is at the forefront of creating environmental awareness and sustainability in Nigeria. The college's core mandate is to train middle-level manpower in forestry and environmental related disciplines for sustenance and development of forestry and agriculture in Nigeria, with focus on tropical rainforest and humid forest zone management. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in forestry technology through National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes in forestry and environmental related disciplines; (b) to train forestry technicians and technologists in sustainable tropical forest management; (c) to provide education and training in environmental management, forest conservation and biodiversity protection in rainforest ecosystems; (d) to train personnel in forest resource assessment, inventory, monitoring and tropical timber management; (e) to provide training in agroforestry suitable for humid zones, forest plantation establishment and management of indigenous tree species; (f) to educate students in wildlife management, biodiversity conservation and protected area management in rainforest ecosystems; (g) to train personnel in wood science, forest products technology, timber processing and non-timber forest product utilization; (h) to provide training in forest nursery management, propagation techniques and tree improvement for tropical species; (i) to educate students in forest protection, pest and disease management relevant to humid tropical environments; (j) to train personnel in community forestry, participatory forest management and forest extension services; (k) to offer wide variety of forestry and environmental related programmes geared toward equipping students in modern technologies and practices; (l) to conduct applied research in forestry and environmental management for tropical forest ecosystems; and (m) to award National Diploma and Higher National Diploma certificates with graduates duly mobilized for National Youth Service Corps.

The Federal College of Forestry Ibadan is a pioneer forestry education institution in Nigeria operated by the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) under Federal Ministry of Environment. Located at Jericho, Ibadan, Oyo State, the college operates as a monotechnic institution approved by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) offering National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) in Forestry Technology and related disciplines. FRIN was established in 1954 as Federal Department of Forestry Research, with status changed to an institute in 1977, retaining aspects of forestry research and education as federal responsibility even after regional administrative divisions. The college's core mandate is to produce technical manpower effecting sustainable development of forestry in Nigeria and Africa, and to serve as credible reference in all matters of forestry education, training and research. Specific functions include: (a) to train technicians and technologists for agricultural, wood, forest and environmental services through full-time and part-time ND and HND programmes; (b) to provide education in forestry technology, forest management and silviculture; (c) to train personnel in wood science, timber technology and forest products utilization; (d) to provide training in forest nursery management, tree breeding and seed technology; (e) to educate students in agroforestry, plantation forestry and social forestry; (f) to train personnel in wildlife management, ecotourism and biodiversity conservation; (g) to provide training in forest protection, pest management and fire ecology; (h) to educate students in forest mensuration, inventory and remote sensing applications; (i) to train personnel in forest economics, policy and community forestry; (j) to conduct forestry research and development; (k) to produce men and women with scientific knowledge necessary to rebuild threatened forest resources through appropriate management technology; (l) to maintain curriculum designed to foster intellectual and practical growth; (m) to provide extensive laboratory and field practical training; and (n) to offer safe, nurturing educational environment with dedicated lecturers and extracurricular activities supporting well-rounded education. The college maintains admission requirements of JAMB UTME minimum score of 100 for ND programmes.

The Federal College of Forestry Jos is a federal tertiary institution operated by Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) under Federal Ministry of Environment, located in Jos, Plateau State. Operating as a monotechnic institution approved by National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), the college offers National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) programmes in forestry technology and environmental related disciplines. The college serves as the forestry education institution for the North-Central geo-political zone and Middle Belt region, with particular focus on montane, guinea savannah and plateau ecosystem management. The college's core mandate is to produce men and women with scientific knowledge necessary to rebuild the population of threatened forest resources of the country through appropriate management technology, and to train technicians and technologists for agricultural, wood, forest and environmental services. Specific functions include: (a) to provide specialized training in forestry technology through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma programmes; (b) to train forestry technicians and technologists in sustainable forest management appropriate for plateau and savannah ecosystems; (c) to provide education and training in environmental management, watershed management and soil conservation for highland areas; (d) to train personnel in forest resource assessment, inventory and monitoring for diverse ecosystems; (e) to provide training in agroforestry systems, plantation forestry and farm forestry suitable for Middle Belt region; (f) to educate students in wildlife management, rangeland management and biodiversity conservation in savannah and montane ecosystems; (g) to train personnel in wood science, timber technology and forest products processing; (h) to provide training in forest nursery management, tree breeding and selection of species suitable for highland and savannah zones; (i) to educate students in forest protection, fire management and pest control; (j) to train personnel in community forestry, extension services and participatory forest management; (k) to conduct applied research in forestry and environmental management for plateau and Middle Belt ecosystems; (l) to provide training in land degradation control, erosion management and environmental restoration; and (m) to award certificates preparing graduates for National Youth Service Corps mobilization and professional forestry careers.

mda_name: 120. FEDERAL COLLEGE OF FRESH WATER FISHERIES - BAGA
mandate_description: The Federal College of Freshwater Fisheries Technology Baga, Borno State, was established by Federal Government of Nigeria under Lake Chad Research Institute in 1977 as a monotechnic institution to provide middle-level manpower in fisheries for Lake Chad basin. Originally established by proxy of Research Institute Order of 1975 (Supplement to Official Gazette No. 61, Vol. 62 of 11th December 1975 Part B) which established Lake Chad Research Institute as parent institute, the college is now under supervision of National Institute for Freshwater Fisheries Research (NIFFR), New Bussa, Niger State, following major reorganization of research institutes nationwide between 1988-1989. Located along Lake Chad shores in Baga, characterized by highly productive lake with historical irrational exploitation and inadequate knowledge of harvesting, preservation, processing and storage, the college admitted first students in 1979 for Vocational Competency in Fisheries, with immediate view of upgrading to OND and eventually HND. National Board for Technical Education halted further OND admission in 1989 pending appreciable upgrade of facilities and personnel, regularized with approval to mount Pre-ND (2008), ND (2010), and HND (2013) programmes in Fisheries Technology. The college's core mandate is to produce middle and lower level manpower in fisheries including fisheries artisans, aquaculture assistants, fisheries technicians and fisheries technologists capable of applying modern fisheries technology to boost fish production on sustainable level. Specific functions include: (a) to train junior, intermediate and senior fisheries personnel for inland fisheries development through short and long term formal education; (b) to train and retrain middle-level manpower in aquaculture technology; (c) to encourage women participation in fisheries through post-harvest technology training; (d) to train food technicians, technologists and chemical analysts in preservation, processing, packaging, storage and marketing of food commodities and equipment; (e) to train agricultural extension technicians to carry out extension work among rural farmers and fisher folks; (f) to provide training in fish farming, hatchery management and pond construction; (g) to educate students in fish biology, aquatic ecology and limnology; (h) to train personnel in fishing gear technology, boat building and fish capture methods; and (i) to be role model for fisheries, agricultural and allied tertiary institutions developing highly intellectual, skilled, creative and self-employable individuals through modern scientific, technological, research and development methods for socio-economic and political growth toward national development goals.

mda_name:
81. Federal College of Agriculture, Ishiagu
**MDA Code:** 215023001
mandate_description:
Following accreditation by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) in 1989, the institution became the Federal College of Agriculture, Umudike. Administrative autonomy was granted by the Federal Government in 1991, and the college was relocated to Ishiagu in 1993 following the establishment of a Federal University on its Umudike campus.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college has the national mandate to develop and organise high-quality, practically oriented training with dynamic curricula to produce self-reliant technicians and technologists at National Diploma and Higher National Diploma levels. Its functions include promoting agricultural training, production, and research in Nigeria; providing extension education and services; integrating system-wide innovations to achieve tangible results; pursuing sustainable capacity building, consultancy, and innovative outreach; increasing agricultural productivity for food security; reducing poverty and unemployment; and securing livelihoods through sustainable agriculture and human development to meet national and global challenges. The college collaborates with the National Root Crops Research Institute, Umudike, for research endeavours and offers NBTE-accredited programmes preparing graduates eligible for NYSC participation.

mda_name:
82. Federal College of Agriculture, Moore Plantation, Ibadan
**MDA Code:** 215022001
mandate_description:
The institution is supervised by the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development through the Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria established by Act 44 of May 26, 1999.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The mandate is to produce diplomats at both National Diploma and Higher National Diploma levels with high academic standards and sound practical skills to meet the demands of the agricultural sector. The college aims to contribute towards achieving Nigeria's goals in agriculture through qualitative education and production of well-equipped middle-level manpower. Core functions include providing qualitative agricultural education including vocational and entrepreneurial training; enhancing agricultural production; serving as a hub for middle-level manpower development in agriculture; providing hands-on training to practically equip students for agricultural processes from input to production and value addition towards food security. Academic programmes span Agricultural Extension and Management, Agricultural Environment and Bio-Engineering, Home and Rural Economics, Horticulture, Animal Production Technology, and related fields.

mda_name:
83. Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology, Ibadan
**MDA Code:** 265004001
mandate_description:
**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is to produce well-trained and morally sound graduates to become self-employed in the areas of Science and Agriculture. It aims to produce graduates at National Diploma and Higher National Diploma levels to meet the needs of farmers, agro-allied industries, pharmaceutical companies, and government agencies. Core functions include: producing technicians capable of carrying out routine preventive measures and advisory services in livestock, fishery, and crop production; establishing linkages and collaboration with policy makers, research institutes, and training institutions; enabling graduates to establish and manage modern standard livestock farms, veterinary clinics, and diagnostic laboratories; promoting capacity building through outreach programmes, vocational training, and continuous education; and promoting youth development and empowerment opportunities through entrepreneurial and home economics activities. The college is the only Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology in the southern part of Nigeria.

mda_name:
84. Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology, Vom
**MDA Code:** 265005001
mandate_description:
In March 1980, the Veterinary School was formally accorded college status and renamed College of Animal Health and Husbandry with a mandate to award Ordinary and Higher Diplomas. The National Science and Technology Amendment Decree No. 46 of December 30, 1990, gave legal backing to conduct training for technicians and technologists. The college was renamed Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology on January 29, 1991.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college is mandated to train middle-level manpower in Animal Health, Animal Production, Livestock Extension/Management Services, and Vocational Training who can effectively utilise their training to establish and manage livestock farms. Its guiding principles include: improving service to the livestock sector through effective training; training minds to appreciate the significance of animal resources in national development; inculcating the importance of practical self-commitment to the dignity of labour for national self-sufficiency in animal protein production; and producing extension staff who can bring agro-veterinary research and innovation to livestock farmers and feedback farmers' problems to appropriate authorities. Programmes include Pre-ND, ND and HND in Animal Health and Production Technology, HND in Animal Health, HND in Animal Production, HND in Agricultural Extension and Management, and Veterinary Science Laboratory Technology.

mda_name:
85. Federal College of Complementary and Alternative Medicine, Nigeria
**MDA Code:** 521027011
mandate_description:
The institution's academic activities were suspended by the National Universities Commission (NUC) in October 2010 for running degree programmes without mandatory approvals. In 2011, the Federal Ministry of Health suspended the management and instituted an Interim Administrative Team. There are ongoing plans to revive FEDCAM as part of the Federal Government's initiative to integrate traditional medicine into the national healthcare system.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
FEDCAM was established with the mandate to train alternative medicine practitioners in healthcare delivery services; carry out clinical works; provide alternative methods of treating ailments; and conduct research in complementary and alternative medicine. Its functions include training and retraining practitioners of Complementary and Alternative Medicine in Nigeria; researching and developing all aspects of Complementary and Alternative Medicine; contributing to formulating regulatory standards; and supporting integration of complementary and alternative medicine into the mainstream Nigerian healthcare delivery system. The college covers modalities including Homeopathy, Naturopathy, Acupuncture, Osteopathy, and Chiropractic practices.

mda_name:
86. Federal College of Dental Technology and Therapy, Enugu
**MDA Code:** 521016001
mandate_description:
The institution was re-established by Nigerian law via the Federal College of Dental Technology and Therapy (Establishment) Act No. 8 of 2017, which granted the power to award degrees. President Muhammadu Buhari signed the Act on December 5, 2017. In February 2021, the National Universities Commission approved the college to run undergraduate degree programmes in collaboration with Federal University of Technology, Owerri.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college is mandated to provide academic and professional training in dental technology and therapy to meet Nigeria's critical healthcare manpower needs. Under Section 6(a) of the Establishment Act, the college is empowered to award degrees, diplomas, and certificates for courses provided under the Act. Core functions include: producing dental technologists and dental therapists for various medical institutions; providing patient care and continuing education opportunities; contributing research discoveries to improve dental healthcare; offering National Diploma, Higher National Diploma, and Bachelor of Technology degree programmes in dental technology and therapy; and serving as a recognised Centre of Excellence in Africa for dental technology and therapy education. The school was once the only institution training dental technologists and therapists in Nigeria.

mda_name:
87. Federal College of Education (Technical), Keana
**MDA Code:** 517019030
mandate_description:
The college's principal officers (Provost, Registrar, Bursar, and Librarian) were appointed in May 2023. The National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE) has granted approval to run 15 academic programmes across four schools housing 15 departments.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college's mandate is to provide full-time courses of teaching, instruction, and training in technology, applied science, commerce, arts, social sciences, humanities, and management leading to the award of the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) and degrees. Core functions include: training qualified technical and vocational teachers for Nigeria's basic education system and technological development; producing educators with intellectual and professional background adequate for their teaching assignment; fostering adaptability to changing educational and national situations; preparing graduates for contributions to the world of work; conducting research in technical education; and organising workshops, seminars, and in-service courses to update practicing teachers' knowledge.

mda_name:
88. Federal College of Education (Technical), Yauri
**MDA Code:** 517019028
mandate_description:
Kebbi State Government donated Government Day Secondary School, Tondi, Yauri, as the take-off site, along with 149,604 hectares for the permanent site. President Bola Tinubu appointed the pioneer principal officers in March 2025: Prof. Sa'adu Umar as Provost, Mr. Abdullahi Ahmed as Registrar, Dr. Muhammad Yusuf Alkali as Bursar, and Mrs. Maimuna Mohammed Ahmed as Librarian, with tenures of five years each as stipulated in the Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college's mandate is to provide quality teacher education and entrepreneurial skills through cutting-edge technology and research-driven pedagogy; foster academic excellence; and prepare graduates to meet the evolving needs of the workforce while contributing meaningfully to national development. Core functions include: offering full-time courses in teaching, instruction, and training across disciplines including technology, applied science, arts, social sciences, humanities, and management; producing transformative leaders and innovators who drive sustainable development and technological advancement; training skilled educators and technicians for Nigeria's industrial and economic growth; and equipping students with practical, industry-relevant skills for the job market.

mda_name:
89. Federal College of Education, Abeokuta
**MDA Code:** 517019001
mandate_description:
The college moved to its permanent site in 1983 at Osiele along the Abeokuta-Ibadan Road, occupying a land area of 632.95 hectares vested by the Federal Government via Gazette No. 4164 of August 25, 1977. In 2010, the Centre for Degree Programmes (CEDEP) was established following resource assessment by the University of Ibadan and National Universities Commission.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college's primary mandate is to provide full-time courses of teaching, instruction, and training in technology, applied science, commerce, arts, social sciences, humanities, and management; and to carry out research in the development and adaptation of techniques. Core functions include: offering three-year full-time and five-year sandwich courses leading to the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE); producing highly motivated and skilled teachers for Primary, Junior Secondary, and Senior Secondary Schools; providing degree programmes in affiliation with the University of Ibadan and Lagos State University; offering Post Graduate Diploma in Education (PGDE); and providing an all-round total quality teaching, research, and public service environment.

mda_name:
90. Federal College of Education (Technical), Akoka
**MDA Code:** 517019002
mandate_description:
In 1982, the college was renamed Federal College of Education (Technical), Akoka, due to expansion in curricula and courses. The college became a fully autonomous academic institution in 1986 with the promulgation of the Federal College of Education Decree No. 4 of 1986 (as amended in 1993). The college moved to its permanent site along St. Finbarr's College Road, Akoka, in September 1975. It is approved by the National Universities Commission and affiliated with Federal University of Technology, Minna, and University of Benin for degree programmes.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is grooming and producing teachers in technical, vocational, and commercial academic disciplines. Core functions include: producing self-reliant Technical and Vocational Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) graduates grounded in Information and Communication Technology, research, and teaching; preparing students to instruct technical subjects at elementary, secondary, and professional levels; offering NCE programmes in Technical Education, Vocational Education, Science Education, and Business Education; awarding undergraduate degrees through university affiliations; and contributing to the technological and socio-economic development of Nigeria through effective research for sustainable living.

mda_name:
91. Federal College of Education (Technical), Asaba
**MDA Code:** 517019003
mandate_description:
The college has relocated to its permanent site along Asaba/Ibusa Road. It is affiliated with the University of Benin for degree programmes and has been approved for independent degree operations under the Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The basic mission of the college is to improve the quality of Technical Education in Nigeria. Core functions include: training professional teachers in technical, vocational, and commercial academic areas; offering pre-degree, NCE, Professional Diploma in Education (PDE), and degree programmes; running competitive integrated foundation year programmes for students who do not meet standard entry criteria; providing world-class learning facilities with well-equipped laboratories, modern equipment, and innovative technologies; preparing students for the education sector; and fostering excellence in learning through multi-media classrooms and modern libraries. The college comprises the School of Education, School of Business Education, School of Technical Education, School of Vocational Education, and School of Computer and Science Education.

mda_name:
92. Federal College of Education (Technical), Bichi
**MDA Code:** 517019004
mandate_description:
The college is affiliated with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University for its degree programmes. It offers relevant courses and programmes at NCE and degree levels and provides vocational/technical services. The current Provost is Bashir Muhammad Fagge. The college has been approved for independent degree operations under the new Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is to produce specialist teachers in technical, vocational, business, and science subjects for the 9-3-4 system of education. Core functions include: running Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) programmes in Technical, Vocational, Business, Science, and Primary Education Studies; producing qualified and dynamic teachers who can successfully perform teacher roles as enshrined in the National Policy on Education; fitting graduates into the world of work; offering degree programmes in chosen lines of endeavour; ensuring effective and qualitative training of teachers for basic education and rapid technological development of the nation; and providing vocational/technical services to the community.

mda_name:
93. Federal College of Education, Eha-Amufu
**MDA Code:** 517019020
mandate_description:
The site was formerly occupied by the Federal Government-owned Teacher Training College (TTC), Eha-Amufu. Following state creation in 1991, Enugu State Government inherited the college. The Federal Government took over in April 1993 with financial effect from January 1994. Decree No. 4 of 1986, amended by Decree No. 34 of 1993 and Decree No. 6 of 1993, established the Federal College of Education, Eha-Amufu as the 20th Federal College of Education. It is affiliated with the University of Nigeria for degree programmes.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mission is to be a distinguished centre of academic excellence and innovation for pre-service and in-service teacher education as well as efficient and effective management. Core functions include: training students who make significant impact in Nigeria's educational sector; providing academic excellence, vocational education, and high moral training; offering NCE, Degree, and Professional Diploma in Education programmes; establishing a Directorate of Entrepreneurship to equip students with skills for self-reliance and job creation; and conducting research in teacher education. The college has received accreditation from NCCE for 17 academic programmes.

mda_name:
94. Federal College of Education (Technical), Ekiadolor
**MDA Code:** 517019027
mandate_description:
In 2020, the Federal Government announced plans to establish new Federal Colleges of Education, including one using facilities of the defunct Tayo Akpata University of Education in Ekiadolor. In April 2022, the Edo State College of Education was handed over to the Federal Government and became the Federal College of Education (Technical), Ekiadolor. The college opened for students on December 2, 2022, with lectures starting December 19, 2022. Pioneer Principal Officers include Dr. Emmanuel Nkoro Asagha (Provost), Mr. Henry O. Itedjere (Registrar), Mr. Solomon Ediae (Bursar), and Dr. Tony Obaseki (College Librarian).

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is to establish a citadel of learning for Technical and Vocational Education Training (TVET). Core functions include: producing disciplined and qualified teachers for enhancement of Technical and Vocational Education Training; ensuring professionalism in Technical and Vocational Education in Nigeria; encouraging advancement of research in TVET among teachers; providing high-quality training empowering students with relevant skills and attitudes in advancing technical and entrepreneurial knowledge; fostering innovation and lifelong learning culture; awarding the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) to graduates; augmenting the shortfall of teachers; and meeting learning, research, and instructional needs of host communities and Nigeria as a whole.

mda_name:
95. Federal College of Education, Gidan Madi
**MDA Code:** 517019022
mandate_description:
The college started academic activities in 2023 with eight programmes and matriculated 287 pioneer students during its maiden matriculation ceremony. Prof. Faruk Umar-Zaki serves as Provost. Plans are underway to expand programmes to complete the School of Vocational and Technical Education and School of Science Education.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is the production of teachers with intellectual and professional background adequate for their assignment and adaptable to changing situations in Nigeria and the world. Core functions include: providing a conducive environment with standard, modern facilities; engaging competent and skillful manpower; enrolling young people for practical training, intellectual development, and behavioural transformation in education delivery; adequately addressing educational sector needs of respective communities; training skilled, disciplined, and responsible educators committed to serving humanity; offering programmes in Metalwork Technology, Woodwork Technology, Electrical and Electronics, Computer Science, Business Education, Computer Education, Mathematics, Physics, and planned expansions in Automobile Technology, Building Technology, Agricultural Science, and Home Economics.

mda_name:
96. Federal College of Education (Technical), Gombe
**MDA Code:** 517019005
mandate_description:
The college is affiliated with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University and the University of Maiduguri for degree programmes. The college has been approved for independent degree operations under the Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023. The current Provost is Dr. Aliyu Adamu, who also serves as Chairman of the Committee of Federal Colleges of Education in Nigeria.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate since inception has been producing technical, vocational, and science teachers for primary and secondary schools. Core functions include: preparing students to acquire Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) over a three-year programme; providing full-time courses in sciences, vocational education, arts, social sciences, and professional preparation of teachers; organising workshops, seminars, conferences, and in-service courses to update practicing teachers' knowledge; striving to be a Centre of Excellence producing highly qualified, competent, and motivated Science, Vocational, and Technical teachers for Nigeria's basic education levels; and cultivating a vibrant learning environment encouraging creativity, innovation, and collaboration. The college comprises six schools: Education, Vocational Education, Business Education, Technical Education, Science Education, and Primary Education Studies.

mda_name:
97. Federal College of Education (Technical), Gusau
**MDA Code:** 517019006
mandate_description:
The college has a unique distinction as the only institution in Africa specifically established for training women technical teachers. It was founded to encourage women to take up technical and vocational subjects for the Nigeria Certificate in Education. The college has graduated over 5,000 women NCE graduates since establishment, with current female-only student enrolment exceeding 7,000. It is affiliated with Federal University Gusau for degree programmes.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is to train and graduate competent female technology teachers and potential entrepreneurs for technological and national development. Core functions include: producing specialist teachers in technical, vocational, business, and science subjects for the education system; encouraging women to participate in technical and vocational fields; offering NCE programmes in Electrical/Electronics Technology, Computer Science, Fine and Applied Arts, Home Economics, Physical and Health Education, and other technical subjects; providing professional diploma programmes; and supporting the training of female technical educators for Nigeria's development needs. The college offers both NCE and degree programmes under its dual mandate.

mda_name:
98. Federal College of Education, Gwoza
**MDA Code:** 517019029
mandate_description:
Governor Babagana Zulum allocated Government Secondary School, Vile, Gwoza, as the temporary site in July 2023. President Bola Tinubu approved the immediate take-off in March 2024. On December 5, 2024, Governor Zulum handed over a completely remodeled edifice as the permanent site to the Federal Ministry of Education, along with a N200 million donation towards the college's take-off.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college was established with a visionary mandate to advance, strengthen, and democratise access to teacher education across Nigeria, addressing persistent barriers hindering Nigerians from obtaining quality professional training in education. Core functions include: providing and promoting sound basic education training as a foundation for national development, taking into account indigenous culture and enhancing national unity; providing higher education fostering systematic advancement of the science and art of teacher education; providing instruction in various branches of teacher education for research advancement and knowledge dissemination; offering NCE programmes in English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, TVET courses, and subjects creating wealth and accelerating development; and encouraging parents in insurgency-affected areas to send children to school through quality educational opportunities.

mda_name:
99. Federal College of Education, Ididep, Ibiono
**MDA Code:** 517019032
mandate_description:
Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State granted a N95 million waiver for the Certificate of Occupancy in September 2023 to facilitate immediate take-off. The Akwa Ibom State Government officially handed over the Certificate of Occupancy to the Federal Government. The college is set on 94.927 hectares of land acquired by the Federal Government, and the affected Ididep community is receiving compensation.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mission is to become a global hub of academic excellence, focusing on innovative teaching, cutting-edge research, and training of motivated educators prepared to excel in various areas of specialisation. Core functions include: producing skilled and passionate teachers for foundational and basic education sectors; offering NCE programmes in Early Childhood Care and Education, English and Ibibio Languages, Christian Religious Studies, Social Studies, Mathematics, Computer Education, Business Education, and Agricultural Education; providing quality training with federal accreditation and quality assurance; creating opportunities for degree progression; and contributing to educational development in Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria at large. The college emphasises academic quality, discipline, and national development through professional teacher training.

mda_name:
100. Federal College of Education, Ilawe-Ekiti
**MDA Code:** 517019033
mandate_description:
The permanent site, also along Ilawe-Ikere Road, covers 107.813 hectares of land donated by the Ilawe community. The official handover of the temporary and permanent sites occurred on November 13, 2023. Dr. Gbade Ikuejube was appointed as the pioneer Provost. The Alawe of Ilawe-Ekiti, Oba Adebanji Ajibade Alabi, and the community celebrated the establishment as fulfillment of a great dream.

**Core Mandate and Functions:**
The college mandate is to promote the production of qualified teachers at the foundational and basic segment of the education sector. It is designed as a two-in-one institution serving as both a College of Education and University, awarding both NCE Certificate and Degrees. Core functions include: running courses in Education, Sciences, and Technology; extending programmes to vocational and allied studies to produce job creators; equipping future educators with knowledge, skills, and professional values for effective teaching; offering NCE programmes across six schools: School of Arts and Social Sciences, School of Early Childhood Care and Primary Education, School of General Education, School of Languages, School of Science, and School of Vocational and Technical Education; and demonstrating the Federal Government's determination to expand educational opportunities and invest in training future educators.

**MDA Code:** 256001001

The Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy (FMACTCE) was established on August 21, 2023, by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, carved out from the Federal Ministry of Information and Culture. On October 23, 2024, it was consolidated through merger with the Federal Ministry of Tourism. The Ministry is led by Hannatu Musa Musawa as Minister. The Ministry launched "Destination 2030, Nigeria Everywhere" on November 21, 2023, targeting 10% GDP contribution from creative sector by 2030 and creation of 2 million jobs by 2027. The Ministry oversees 13 agencies including National Theatre (renamed Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts in July 2024), National Gallery of Arts, National Commission for Museums and Monuments, National Institute for Cultural Orientation, National Council for Arts and Culture, and Nigerian Copyright Commission.

**Core Mandate:** To promote and develop arts, culture, creative industries and tourism, using creativity to boost economy, preserve cultural heritage and share Nigeria's culture globally.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Create enabling environment encouraging artistic excellence, promoting diversity and creativity
(b) Preserve Nigeria's rich cultural heritage across 371 tribes and over 250 ethnic groups
(c) Facilitate economic diversification through creative economy, wealth creation and value addition
(d) Implement Destination 2030 initiative targeting $100 billion GDP increase by 2030
(e) Develop and implement National Tourism Policy and National Tourism Masterplan
(f) Promote public-private partnerships for tourism infrastructure development
(g) Enhance tourist sites, train professional tour guides and promote community-based tourism
(h) Support artists, cultural groups and creative businesses
(i) Position Nigeria as premier destination for cultural tourism
(j) Renovate and maintain cultural institutions including National Theatre and cultural centers
(k) Promote Nigerian music, film (Nollywood), fashion, literature and visual arts globally
(l) Protect intellectual property rights of Nigerian creatives through Nigerian Copyright Commission
(m) Organize cultural festivals, exhibitions and events showcasing Nigeria's heritage
(n) Develop creative hubs and incubation centers supporting creative entrepreneurs
(o) Collaborate with state governments, private sector and international partners

mda_name: 162. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF AVIATION AND AEROSPACE DEVELOPMENT - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development regulates air travel and aviation services in Nigeria. The Ministry was renamed from Federal Ministry of Aviation to include "Aerospace Development" reflecting expanded mandate. Current Minister is Festus Keyamo, CON, SAN, FCIArb (UK), appointed August 16, 2023. Permanent Secretary is Dr. Ibrahim Abubakar Kana, mni. Headquarters located at Federal Secretariat Complex Phase 1, Abuja. The Ministry operates under Five-Point Agenda: (1) ensuring strict compliance with safety regulations and continuous upward movement of Nigeria's ICAO rating; (2) supporting growth of local airline businesses; (3) infrastructure improvement; (4) human capacity development; (5) revenue optimization. The Ministry oversees Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT) Zaria, Accident Investigation Bureau (AIB), Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), and African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU).

**Core Mandate:** To build safe, secured and efficient aviation industry making Nigeria hub meeting international standards and best practices for African continent.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and manage government policies and programmes on aviation and aerospace development
(b) Oversee air transportation including licensing, regulations and operational standards for airlines
(c) Oversee airport development and management through FAAN
(d) Provide aviation infrastructural services including runways, terminals, navigation aids
(e) Provide aviation security services meeting international standards
(f) Improve airspace management and air traffic control through automation and next-generation systems
(g) Ensure safety and security measures comply with ICAO standards and WMO requirements
(h) Regulate civil aviation operations ensuring adherence to safety protocols
(i) Develop and maintain meteorological services for aviation through NiMet
(j) Investigate aircraft accidents and incidents through AIB
(k) Develop human capacity through Nigerian College of Aviation Technology
(l) Certify aerodrome emergency training schools and firefighting facilities
(m) Support growth and sustainability of local airline businesses
(n) Optimize revenue generation from aviation sector
(o) Modernize airport terminals and expand cargo and logistics networks
(p) Position Nigeria as leading aviation hub in Africa
(q) Develop aerospace education and research through African Aviation and Aerospace University

mda_name: 163. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF BUDGET AND ECONOMIC PLANNING - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning (formerly Federal Ministry of Budget and National Planning) is responsible for national budget preparation, economic planning, development policy formulation and coordination of national development plans. Restructured and renamed under President Bola Tinubu's administration to emphasize integrated approach to budget formulation and economic planning. The Ministry serves as central coordinating agency for Nigeria's development planning and budget management. It oversees National Bureau of Statistics, National Planning Commission, and coordinates implementation of national development frameworks including Economic Recovery and Growth Plan successors.

**Core Mandate:** To formulate, coordinate and monitor implementation of national economic development policies, plans and programmes, and prepare annual national budget.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Prepare Federal Government annual budget and Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF)
(b) Formulate national development plans including National Development Plan and sector strategies
(c) Coordinate economic planning across all ministries, departments and agencies
(d) Monitor and evaluate implementation of government policies, programmes and projects
(e) Conduct macroeconomic analysis and forecasting for policy planning
(f) Advise Federal Government on economic policy directions and development priorities
(g) Coordinate national statistical system and data collection for planning
(h) Prepare Economic Recovery and Growth Plan and successor economic frameworks
(i) Oversee National Bureau of Statistics for data generation and analysis
(j) Coordinate donor-funded projects and development partner relationships
(k) Manage Nigeria's development cooperation with bilateral and multilateral partners
(l) Prepare national investment plans attracting public and private investments
(m) Coordinate implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Nigeria
(n) Conduct project appraisals and feasibility studies for major government projects
(o) Allocate capital expenditure across sectors based on national priorities
(p) Monitor budget performance and expenditure tracking
(q) Coordinate poverty reduction strategies and social development programmes
(r) Develop infrastructure investment frameworks and industrial development policies

mda_name: 164. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND DIGITAL ECONOMY HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy (formerly Federal Ministry of Communications Technology) is responsible for communications infrastructure, telecommunications regulation, digital economy development, information technology, postal services and broadcasting. Renamed to reflect Nigeria's strategic focus on leveraging digital technologies for economic transformation and positioning Nigeria as digital economy hub in Africa. The Ministry coordinates Nigeria's digital transformation agenda and oversees Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST), National Broadcasting Commission (NBC), and manages spectrum allocation and universal service provision.

**Core Mandate:** To facilitate development of communications sector, promote digital economy growth, ensure universal access to communications services and position Nigeria as technology-driven economy.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national communications and digital economy policies
(b) Oversee telecommunications sector development and regulation through NCC
(c) Promote broadband penetration and universal telecommunications access
(d) Develop National Broadband Plan and ensure its implementation
(e) Promote digital economy development and digital entrepreneurship
(f) Facilitate e-government services and digital public services delivery
(g) Oversee National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) for IT sector development
(h) Regulate information technology practices and data protection through NITDA
(i) Promote software development, ICT innovation and technology startups
(j) Develop national cybersecurity framework and coordinate cybersecurity initiatives
(k) Oversee postal services through Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST)
(l) Regulate broadcasting services through National Broadcasting Commission (NBC)
(m) Promote local content development in ICT sector
(n) Facilitate digital skills acquisition and ICT literacy programmes
(o) Promote e-commerce development and digital payment systems
(p) Coordinate spectrum management and allocation
(q) Promote rural telecommunications access through Universal Service Provision Fund
(r) Facilitate public-private partnerships in ICT infrastructure development
(s) Develop frameworks for emerging technologies including AI, IoT, blockchain and cloud computing
(t) Coordinate national identity management through NIMC

The Federal Ministry of Education is responsible for formulating, coordinating and monitoring national education policies, overseeing federal education institutions and ensuring quality education delivery at all levels. The Ministry provides policy direction for Nigeria's education sector encompassing basic education, secondary education, tertiary education and special education. Led by Minister of Education assisted by Ministers of State and Permanent Secretary, the Ministry supervises federal universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, unity schools (Federal Government Colleges) and specialized educational institutions while coordinating with state and local governments. Key regulatory agencies under the Ministry include National Universities Commission (NUC), National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE), Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), National Commission for Nomadic Education (NCNE), and National Commission for Mass Literacy, Adult and Non-Formal Education.

**Core Mandate:** To formulate and implement policies ensuring qualitative and functional education for all Nigerians, coordinating education sector development at federal level.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate national education policy including National Policy on Education and ensure implementation
(b) Oversee federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education
(c) Regulate establishment and accreditation of tertiary institutions through NUC, NBTE and NCCE
(d) Coordinate Unity Schools (Federal Government Colleges) nationwide
(e) Supervise Federal Science and Technical Colleges
(f) Coordinate nomadic education through National Commission for Nomadic Education
(g) Promote adult and non-formal education through National Commission for Mass Literacy
(h) Oversee special education for persons with disabilities
(i) Coordinate basic education programmes through Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC)
(j) Regulate examinations and certifications through examination bodies
(k) Develop curriculum frameworks and approve curricula for federal institutions
(l) Ensure quality assurance in education through monitoring and evaluation
(m) Coordinate teacher education and professional development
(n) Manage scholarship programmes including Federal Government scholarships and bursaries
(o) Promote educational research and development
(p) Coordinate educational infrastructure development in federal institutions
(q) Facilitate access, equity and inclusion in education
(r) Promote girl-child education and gender equality
(s) Develop and implement educational technology and e-learning frameworks
(t) Coordinate education sector development plans and budgets

The Federal Ministry of Environment is responsible for environmental protection, conservation, pollution control, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and sustainable environmental management. Established to address environmental challenges including deforestation, desertification, erosion, pollution, biodiversity loss and climate change impacts. Led by Minister of Environment assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA), Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN), National Oil Spills Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA), Great Green Wall Agency, Nigerian Conservation Foundation, and coordinates Nigeria's implementation of international environmental conventions including UNFCCC, Convention on Biological Diversity, Montreal Protocol and Ramsar Convention.

**Core Mandate:** To facilitate sustainable management of Nigeria's environment and natural resources for present and future generations, addressing environmental degradation and climate change.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national environmental policies including National Environmental Policy
(b) Coordinate environmental protection and conservation programmes
(c) Enforce environmental laws and regulations through NESREA
(d) Conduct environmental impact assessments for major development projects
(e) Coordinate climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies through Climate Change Department
(f) Implement Nigeria's Nationally Determined Contributions under Paris Agreement
(g) Coordinate desertification control and Great Green Wall initiative in northern Nigeria
(h) Manage erosion control and watershed management programmes
(i) Coordinate forest resources management and conservation through FRIN
(j) Promote afforestation and reforestation programmes
(k) Manage biodiversity conservation and protected areas
(l) Coordinate pollution control (air, water, soil) and waste management
(m) Regulate and respond to oil spills through NOSDRA
(n) Coordinate environmental emergencies and disasters response
(o) Promote renewable energy and clean energy technologies
(p) Manage Nigeria's obligations under international environmental conventions
(q) Conduct environmental monitoring and reporting
(r) Promote environmental education and public awareness
(s) Regulate pesticides and industrial chemicals
(t) Facilitate green economy initiatives and sustainable production patterns

The Federal Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing Nigeria's public finances, revenue generation, fiscal policy formulation, debt management and economic stabilization. The Ministry coordinates government revenue collection, budget execution, financial regulations and macroeconomic stability. Operating under Minister of Finance (appointed by President, often titled Coordinating Minister for the Economy), the Ministry supervises Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS), Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Debt Management Office (DMO), Budget Office of the Federation, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), Pension Commission (PenCom), Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), and other financial sector regulators. The Ministry manages Nigeria's relationships with international financial institutions including World Bank, IMF and African Development Bank.

**Core Mandate:** To efficiently manage Nigeria's financial resources, promote economic growth and ensure fiscal sustainability.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national fiscal and financial policies
(b) Coordinate revenue generation through tax administration, customs duties and non-oil revenues
(c) Oversee Federal Inland Revenue Service for tax collection and administration
(d) Manage Nigeria Customs Service for customs duties collection and border control
(e) Prepare and execute Federal Government annual budget
(f) Manage government expenditure and treasury operations
(g) Coordinate public debt management through Debt Management Office
(h) Negotiate external borrowing and manage debt portfolio
(i) Oversee capital market development through Securities and Exchange Commission
(j) Regulate financial reporting and corporate governance
(k) Manage government investments and shareholdings
(l) Coordinate fiscal federalism and revenue allocation to states and local governments
(m) Administer Excess Crude Account and sovereign wealth funds
(n) Manage foreign exchange reserves and exchange rate policies
(o) Coordinate pension fund management and administration
(p) Regulate microfinance and financial inclusion programmes
(q) Oversee insurance industry regulation through NAICOM
(r) Manage government accounting and financial reporting standards
(s) Coordinate public procurement policies
(t) Promote investment climate reforms and ease of doing business
(u) Ensure macroeconomic stability and counter-cyclical fiscal policies

mda_name: 168. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND SOCIAL WELFARE - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare was created through merger in October 2024 cabinet reshuffle, combining Federal Ministry of Health with social welfare and humanitarian functions. The Ministry is responsible for national health policies, healthcare delivery systems, disease control, pharmaceutical regulation, social welfare programmes and humanitarian services. Led by Minister of Health and Social Welfare assisted by Ministers of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry coordinates Nigeria's health sector encompassing primary healthcare, secondary healthcare, tertiary healthcare, public health, reproductive health and nutrition. Key agencies include National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA), Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Teaching Hospitals, Federal Medical Centres, Federal Psychiatric Hospitals, and social welfare agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To ensure health for all Nigerians through formulation and implementation of health and social welfare policies, coordinating healthcare delivery and protecting vulnerable populations.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national health policies including National Health Policy
(b) Coordinate primary healthcare development through NPHCDA
(c) Oversee federal tertiary hospitals including Teaching Hospitals, Federal Medical Centres
(d) Regulate pharmaceuticals, food and medical products through NAFDAC
(e) Coordinate disease surveillance and epidemic response through NCDC
(f) Manage public health programmes including immunization, malaria control, TB control, HIV/AIDS
(g) Implement National Health Insurance Scheme promoting universal health coverage
(h) Coordinate reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health programmes
(i) Manage nutrition interventions and food security programmes
(j) Regulate medical and health professions through professional councils
(k) Coordinate health workforce development and training
(l) Manage health infrastructure development in federal health facilities
(m) Coordinate emergency medical services and disaster health response
(n) Implement International Health Regulations compliance and global health security
(o) Coordinate social welfare programmes for vulnerable groups
(p) Manage social protection schemes and safety net programmes
(q) Coordinate humanitarian response for internally displaced persons and refugees
(r) Implement child protection services and prevent violence against children
(s) Coordinate poverty alleviation interventions
(t) Manage health information systems and data management

mda_name: 169. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development (separated from former Ministry of Works and Housing) is responsible for formulating and implementing housing policies, urban development strategies, physical planning and housing finance. Established to address Nigeria's massive housing deficit estimated at 28 million units, the Ministry promotes affordable housing access, regulates urban development and coordinates urban renewal programmes. Led by Minister of Housing and Urban Development assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), Urban Development Bank, and coordinates with state governments on housing programmes. The Ministry implements National Housing Fund, National Housing Policy, and Presidential Housing Initiatives.

**Core Mandate:** To facilitate access to decent and affordable housing for all Nigerians, promote sustainable urban development and regulate physical planning.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national housing policies including National Housing Policy
(b) Develop and implement national housing programmes for affordable housing delivery
(c) Oversee Federal Housing Authority for mass housing development and estate management
(d) Coordinate Federal Mortgage Bank operations for housing finance and mortgage lending
(e) Promote National Housing Fund for workers' housing finance
(f) Develop housing finance mechanisms including mortgage insurance schemes
(g) Formulate urban development policies and sustainable urbanization strategies
(h) Coordinate urban renewal and slum upgrading programmes
(i) Regulate physical planning and urban development standards
(j) Promote building standards and construction codes compliance
(k) Coordinate land use planning and zoning regulations at federal level
(l) Develop urban infrastructure supporting housing estates
(m) Promote public-private partnerships in housing development
(n) Coordinate social housing programmes for low-income earners
(o) Develop housing cooperatives and self-help housing schemes
(p) Promote green building practices and sustainable housing technologies
(q) Coordinate housing research and development including building materials research
(r) Regulate real estate development and construction industry practices
(s) Manage federal government housing estates and quarters
(t) Coordinate housing data collection and housing needs assessment

mda_name: 170. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF HUMANITARIAN AFFAIRS AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Alleviation (established 2019 as Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs, Disaster Management and Social Development, renamed to emphasize poverty alleviation, later merged with Health Ministry in October 2024 but previously operational as standalone) was responsible for humanitarian response, disaster management, internally displaced persons assistance, refugees management, social development and poverty alleviation programmes. The Ministry coordinated Nigeria's humanitarian interventions particularly in North-East affected by Boko Haram insurgency and implemented National Social Investment Programmes. When operational, it supervised National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons, and managed social investment programmes including N-Power, Conditional Cash Transfer, Government Enterprise and Empowerment Programme (GEEP), and Home-Grown School Feeding.

**Core Mandate (when operational):** To coordinate humanitarian assistance, manage disaster response, protect vulnerable populations and implement poverty alleviation interventions.

**Statutory Functions (when operational):**
(a) Coordinate humanitarian response for conflict-affected and disaster-affected populations
(b) Oversee National Emergency Management Agency for disaster preparedness and response
(c) Coordinate assistance for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in camps and host communities
(d) Manage refugees and migrants through National Commission for Refugees
(e) Implement National Social Investment Programmes including N-Power and Conditional Cash Transfer
(f) Coordinate poverty alleviation interventions targeting extreme poor and vulnerable
(g) Implement social protection programmes and safety nets
(h) Manage humanitarian response in North-East Nigeria
(i) Coordinate reconstruction and rehabilitation in conflict-affected areas
(j) Protect vulnerable groups including children, women, elderly and persons with disabilities
(k) Coordinate with international humanitarian organizations and UN agencies
(l) Manage humanitarian aid distribution and relief materials
(m) Implement livelihood support programmes for vulnerable populations
(n) Coordinate psychosocial support for trauma-affected populations
(o) Manage social registers of poor and vulnerable households
(p) Implement school feeding programmes nationwide
(q) Coordinate youth empowerment and job creation schemes through N-Power
(r) Manage post-disaster recovery and resilience building
(s) Coordinate disaster risk reduction and early warning systems

mda_name: 171. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF INDUSTRY, TRADE AND INVESTMENT - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment is responsible for formulating and implementing policies promoting industrial development, trade facilitation, investment attraction, consumer protection and private sector development. Led by Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment assisted by Ministers of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC), National Office for Technology Acquisition and Promotion (NOTAP), Bank of Industry (BOI), Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN), Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), National Sugar Development Council, Raw Materials Research and Development Council, and Export Processing Zones Authority. The Ministry implements National Industrial Revolution Plan and coordinates Nigeria's participation in African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and ECOWAS trade agreements.

**Core Mandate:** To formulate policies that promote industrial development, facilitate domestic and international trade, attract investments and ensure competitive markets for economic diversification and growth.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national industrial policies including National Industrial Revolution Plan
(b) Promote industrialization and manufacturing sector development
(c) Oversee Standards Organisation of Nigeria for quality standards and metrology
(d) Coordinate investment promotion and facilitation through NIPC
(e) Implement ease of doing business reforms and investment climate improvements
(f) Regulate business registration through Corporate Affairs Commission
(g) Promote small and medium enterprises development through SMEDAN
(h) Facilitate access to industrial finance through Bank of Industry
(i) Coordinate export promotion and trade development through NEPC
(j) Promote non-oil exports and export diversification
(k) Facilitate trade policy development and trade negotiations
(l) Coordinate Nigeria's participation in regional trade agreements (ECOWAS, AfCFTA)
(m) Promote foreign direct investment attraction and retention
