(n) Coordinate technology transfer and acquisition through NOTAP
(o) Promote industrial clusters and special economic zones development
(p) Oversee competition policy and consumer protection through FCCPC
(q) Coordinate value chain development for priority commodities
(r) Promote backward integration policies in key sectors
(s) Coordinate industrial parks and free trade zones development
(t) Facilitate supply chain development and local content policies

mda_name: 172. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND NATIONAL ORIENTATION - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation (renamed from Federal Ministry of Information in October 2024 cabinet reshuffle, previously Federal Ministry of Information and Culture before Arts, Culture and Creative Economy was separated in 2023) is responsible for government communication, public information dissemination, national orientation, media regulation, public enlightenment and national integration. Led by Minister of Information and National Orientation assisted by Permanent Secretary, the Ministry serves as Federal Government's communication hub managing official information flow. The Ministry supervises Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN), Voice of Nigeria (VON), News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), National Broadcasting Commission (NBC), National Orientation Agency (NOA), Nigerian Press Council, Advertising Practitioners Council of Nigeria (APCON), and National Film and Video Censors Board.

**Core Mandate:** To provide timely and accurate information about government policies, programmes and activities to citizens, promote national unity and cohesion, and facilitate democratic governance through transparent communication.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Disseminate information about Federal Government policies, programmes and activities
(b) Coordinate government communication strategy and official government statements
(c) Oversee Nigerian Television Authority for public broadcasting services
(d) Manage Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria for radio broadcasting
(e) Coordinate Voice of Nigeria for international broadcasting promoting Nigeria's image
(f) Oversee News Agency of Nigeria as national news wire service
(g) Regulate broadcasting industry through National Broadcasting Commission
(h) Coordinate national orientation programmes promoting patriotism through National Orientation Agency
(i) Promote civic education and citizenship responsibilities
(j) Coordinate public enlightenment campaigns on government policies
(k) Regulate advertising practice through APCON
(l) Regulate print media and journalism practice through Nigerian Press Council
(m) Coordinate film censorship and video censorship through National Film and Video Censors Board
(n) Organize press briefings, media engagements and ministerial press conferences
(o) Facilitate media access to government information and officials
(p) Promote press freedom and protect journalists' rights
(q) Coordinate government's digital communication and social media strategy
(r) Promote national integration and inter-ethnic harmony
(s) Counter fake news, misinformation and disinformation
(t) Coordinate national campaigns on critical issues including anti-corruption and peace building

The Federal Ministry of Justice is principal legal adviser to Federal Government of Nigeria, responsible for legal policy formulation, prosecution of federal offences, law reform, administration of justice and international legal affairs. Headed by Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice (appointed by President as chief law officer of Federation under Constitution Section 150), the Ministry operates through Attorney-General's Chambers providing legal services to government. The Ministry supervises Legal Aid Council, Nigerian Law Reform Commission, National Agency for Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Nigerian Correctional Service (formerly Prisons Service), Nigerian Copyright Commission, and Federal Public Complaints Commission (Ombudsman).

**Core Mandate:** To provide legal services to Federal Government, ensure administration of justice, prosecute federal offences, and uphold rule of law.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Serve as principal legal adviser to President and Federal Government
(b) Provide legal opinions and advice to Federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies
(c) Draft legislation, executive orders and legal instruments for government
(d) Represent Federal Government in litigation before all courts and tribunals
(e) Prosecute criminal offences under federal jurisdiction
(f) Oversee Economic and Financial Crimes Commission for anti-corruption enforcement
(g) Coordinate Independent Corrupt Practices Commission for corruption prevention
(h) Manage Nigerian Correctional Service for administration of correctional facilities
(i) Oversee Legal Aid Council providing legal services to indigent citizens
(j) Coordinate law reform through Nigerian Law Reform Commission
(k) Combat human trafficking through NAPTIP
(l) Manage international legal affairs and treaty negotiations
(m) Coordinate Nigeria's participation in international courts and tribunals
(n) Enforce intellectual property rights through Nigerian Copyright Commission
(o) Coordinate legal education and continuing legal education
(p) Manage federal government litigation portfolio
(q) Coordinate administration of criminal justice reforms
(r) Promote alternative dispute resolution mechanisms
(s) Manage extradition proceedings and mutual legal assistance
(t) Promote access to justice and legal empowerment

mda_name: 174. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment is responsible for labour administration, employment services, industrial relations, occupational safety and health, social security and productivity enhancement. Led by Minister of Labour and Employment assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises National Directorate of Employment (NDE), Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Michael Imoudu National Institute for Labour Studies (MINILS), Industrial Training Fund (ITF), Employees Compensation Commission, National Productivity Centre, and registers and regulates trade unions and employers' associations. The Ministry enforces Labour Act, implements minimum wage legislation, mediates industrial disputes and ensures Nigeria's compliance with International Labour Organization (ILO) conventions. The Ministry coordinates tripartite consultations among government, employers and workers.

**Core Mandate:** To facilitate full employment, ensure decent work conditions, promote harmonious industrial relations, enforce labour standards and enhance national productivity.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national labour and employment policies
(b) Regulate employment relationships and enforce labour laws including Labour Act
(c) Promote employment generation through National Directorate of Employment
(d) Manage employment services connecting job seekers with employers
(e) Register and regulate trade unions and workers' organizations
(f) Register and regulate employers' associations
(g) Promote collective bargaining and social dialogue
(h) Mediate and arbitrate industrial disputes preventing and resolving strikes
(i) Enforce minimum wage implementation across sectors
(j) Regulate wages, hours of work and conditions of employment
(k) Enforce occupational safety and health standards
(l) Inspect workplaces ensuring compliance with labour standards
(m) Combat child labour and forced labour
(n) Promote workers' rights and protect vulnerable workers
(o) Administer social security schemes through Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund
(p) Manage employees' compensation for workplace injuries through Employees Compensation Commission
(q) Promote productivity enhancement through National Productivity Centre
(r) Coordinate industrial training and skills development through Industrial Training Fund
(s) Regulate employment of expatriates and work permits
(t) Coordinate tripartite consultations among government, employers and workers

The Federal Ministry of Livestock Development is newly created ministry established in October 2024 by President Bola Tinubu during cabinet reshuffle to address persistent farmer-herder conflicts, modernize livestock sector and promote livestock industry development. Previously livestock development was handled by Department of Livestock under Federal Ministry of Agriculture. The creation of standalone Livestock Ministry represents significant policy shift recognizing livestock sector's economic potential and need for dedicated attention to pastoralism challenges including nomadic herding, grazing routes, cattle rustling, and conflicts between farmers and herders that have caused thousands of deaths. Led by Minister of Livestock Development appointed October 2024. The Ministry is expected to coordinate livestock production, animal health services, ranching development, dairy industry, meat production, pastoral development and implementation of National Livestock Transformation Plan.

**Core Mandate:** To develop and regulate livestock sector, promote modern livestock production systems, resolve farmer-herder conflicts and enhance livestock contribution to national economy and food security.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national livestock development policies
(b) Promote modern livestock production systems replacing open grazing
(c) Develop and implement National Livestock Transformation Plan
(d) Establish livestock grazing reserves and ranches nationwide
(e) Coordinate ranching development and livestock settlements
(f) Resolve farmer-herder conflicts through sustainable grazing solutions

mda_name: 176. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF MARINE AND BLUE ECONOMY - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy is newly created ministry established in August 2023 by President Bola Tinubu to harness Nigeria's maritime resources, develop blue economy and maximize economic potential of Nigeria's 853km coastline, territorial waters, Exclusive Economic Zone and inland waterways. Previously maritime affairs were handled by Federal Ministry of Transportation. The Ministry coordinates development of ocean economy including fisheries, aquaculture, shipping, offshore oil and gas, marine tourism, seabed mining and marine biotechnology. Led by Minister of Marine and Blue Economy appointed 2023 assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry coordinates Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), and implements Cabotage Act promoting indigenous shipping.

**Core Mandate:** To develop and regulate marine resources, promote sustainable blue economy development, ensure maritime security and maximize economic benefits from Nigeria's maritime domain.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement national marine and blue economy policies
(b) Develop blue economy master plan harnessing maritime resources
(c) Coordinate maritime transport and shipping industry development

(e) Promote indigenous shipping and cabotage regime implementation
(f) Regulate ports and port operations through Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA)
(g) Develop port infrastructure and maritime logistics
(h) Coordinate inland waterways development through National Inland Waterways Authority
(i) Promote maritime security and combat piracy, sea robbery and illegal fishing
(j) Coordinate marine fisheries development and aquaculture
(k) Regulate offshore oil and gas operations in territorial waters

mda_name: 177. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF NIGER DELTA HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Niger Delta Affairs was established in 2008 during President Umaru Yar'Adua's administration to address decades of neglect, environmental degradation, youth restiveness, militancy and underdevelopment in oil-rich Niger Delta region comprising nine oil-producing states: Abia, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo, Imo, Ondo and Rivers. Despite contributing over 80% of Nigeria's foreign exchange earnings, the region suffered environmental degradation from oil pollution and gas flaring, poverty, unemployment and insecurity. Led by Minister of Niger Delta Affairs assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary, the Ministry coordinates special interventions complementing Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC). The Ministry implements amnesty programmes for ex-militants, coordinates environmental remediation including Ogoniland cleanup, and facilitates peace building in oil-producing communities.

**Core Mandate:** To coordinate development programmes and projects in Niger Delta region, facilitate peace building, environmental restoration and socio-economic development.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Formulate and implement special development policies for Niger Delta region
(b) Coordinate Federal Government interventions in Niger Delta complementing NDDC

(g) Coordinate scholarships and educational support for Niger Delta students

(s) Coordinate disaster response in flood-prone riverine communities
(t) Facilitate economic diversification beyond oil in Niger Delta

The Federal Ministry of Police Affairs was established in 1999 when President Olusegun Obasanjo separated police affairs from Interior Ministry. The Ministry is responsible for police policy formulation, police welfare, budget management, logistics and support services for Nigeria Police Force, while operational control remains with Inspector-General of Police under Police Act 2020. Led by Minister of Police Affairs assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary, the Ministry serves as liaison between Federal Government and Nigeria Police Force, providing policy guidance and administrative support without interfering in operational command structure. The Ministry manages police budget, procures equipment, develops police infrastructure including barracks and training facilities, and coordinates police reforms.

**Core Mandate:** To formulate policies for effective policing, provide logistical support to Nigeria Police Force, manage police budget and ensure police welfare.

The Federal Ministry of Power is responsible for formulating and implementing policies for power sector development, electricity generation, transmission, distribution, rural electrification and renewable energy. Following Electric Power Sector Reform Act 2005 which liberalized sector and created successor companies to defunct National Electric Power Authority (NEPA/PHCN), the Ministry emerged focusing exclusively on power sector. Led by Minister of Power assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Rural Electrification Agency (REA), Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), and coordinates with privatized generation companies (GenCos) and distribution companies (DisCos). The Ministry implements national grid expansion, promotes renewable energy including solar and wind, coordinates gas-to-power initiatives, and facilitates Nigeria's participation in West African Power Pool.

mda_name: 180. FEDERAL MINISTRY OF SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION - HQTRS
mandate_description:
The Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (renamed from Federal Ministry of Science and Technology to emphasize Innovation under President Buhari's second term, continued by President Tinubu) is responsible for formulating and implementing policies promoting scientific research, technological development, innovation and technology transfer for national development. Led by Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation assisted by Minister of State and Permanent Secretary. The Ministry supervises over 35 research institutes and agencies including National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA), Energy Commission of Nigeria, National Office for Technology Acquisition and Promotion (NOTAP), Raw Materials Research and Development Council, National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), National Biotechnology Development Agency (NABDA), Nigerian Building and Road Research Institute (NBRRI), Federal Institute of Industrial Research Oshodi (FIIRO), and numerous sector-specific research institutes.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Brussels, Belgium, is one of Nigeria's most strategic diplomatic missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Belgium with concurrent accreditation to European Union and Luxembourg. Located in Brussels, Belgium's capital and de facto capital of European Union hosting EU institutions, NATO headquarters and numerous international organizations. Operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the mission holds dual importance managing bilateral Nigeria-Belgium relations and serving as Nigeria's mission to European Union. EU is collectively Nigeria's major trading partner and development cooperation provider. The mission negotiates EU-Nigeria relations including Economic Partnership Agreements, migration management, development aid through European Development Fund, and security cooperation. Belgium itself has colonial history with Congo and expertise in diamond trade relevant to Nigeria. Substantial Nigerian diaspora lives in Belgium including asylum seekers. The mission coordinates Nigeria's engagement with EU institutions on trade, migration, security and development.

**Core Mandate:** To represent Nigeria's interests in Belgium and European Union, coordinate EU engagement, manage migration issues, promote trade and advance Nigeria's European policy.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Bucharest, Romania, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Romania. Located in Bucharest, Romania's capital and largest city, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with Eastern European EU member state. Romania has experienced significant Nigerian irregular migration with many Nigerians seeking EU entry through Romania before Schengen accession. Romanian authorities have deported numerous Nigerians. Some Nigerian students study in Romanian universities attracted by lower costs. Small Nigerian trading community operates in Bucharest. Romania has agricultural expertise and oil refining capacity relevant to Nigeria. As EU member, Romania participates in EU-Africa relations. The mission addresses primarily consular issues and migration management while promoting limited trade ties. Romania's experience with democratic transition and EU accession interests Nigerian governance reforms.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Buea, Cameroon, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Cameroon. Located in Buea, Cameroon's Southwest Region (though Yaoundé is capital), operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Note: Most sources indicate Nigeria's mission to Cameroon is in Yaoundé, not Buea. However, Buea's location in anglophone Southwest Region connects to Nigeria's concerns about Cameroon's anglophone crisis. The mission manages Nigeria's crucial relationship with major eastern neighbor sharing 1,690 km border. Nigeria-Cameroon relations have experienced tensions over Bakassi Peninsula maritime boundary dispute resolved by ICJ in Cameroon's favor. Both countries cooperate extensively on Lake Chad Basin security against Boko Haram. Significant cross-border trade and population movement occurs. Nigerian refugees fled to Cameroon during civil war; Cameroonian refugees flee anglophone crisis to Nigeria. Both countries are ECCAS and Lake Chad Basin Commission members.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Bujumbura, Burundi, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Burundi. Burundi experienced ethnic conflict between Hutu and Tutsi populations resulting in civil war. Political crisis intensified in 2015 when President Nkurunziza sought unconstitutional third term. Burundi's poverty, political instability and regional tensions create difficult operating environment. The mission maintains diplomatic presence monitoring Great Lakes region security dynamics.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Caracas, Venezuela, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Conakry, Guinea, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Guinea (Guinea-Conakry, distinct from Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea). The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with francophone West African neighbor and ECOWAS member. Guinea has vast mineral wealth including bauxite (world's largest reserves), iron ore, gold and diamonds. Nigerian traders operate in Guinean markets. Both countries cooperate in ECOWAS, Mano River Union and West African regional integration. Guinea has experienced political instability including 2021 military coup. Nigeria has role in ECOWAS mediation. Historical ties exist through shared opposition to colonialism. Guinea's mining sector development interests Nigeria. The mission promotes regional integration, monitors political developments and protects Nigerian commercial interests in minerals-rich but politically unstable country.

Cuba historically supported African liberation movements including Angola where Cuban troops fought. Nigeria and Cuba maintain South-South solidarity ties. Cuban medical professionals have worked in Nigeria and other African countries. Cuba has healthcare and biotechnology expertise despite poverty from US sanctions and economic mismanagement. Hong Kong has unique status as Chinese territory with separate customs, legal system and autonomy (until recent Chinese restrictions). Nigerian traders operate in Hong Kong using it as gateway for Asian imports. Hong Kong serves as financial center for Nigerian businesses' Asian operations. Some Nigerians transit through Hong Kong. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Islamabad, Pakistan, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Located in Islamabad, Pakistan's purpose-built capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with major South Asian Muslim country. Significant Nigerian community in Pakistan includes students studying in Pakistani universities, Islamic scholars at madrasas, and pilgrims. Pakistan provides affordable higher education attracting Nigerian students. Both countries cooperate extensively in Organization of Islamic Cooperation and Islamic Development Bank. Pakistan's nuclear program, defense industry and military expertise interests Nigeria. Some Nigerian students have been radicalized in Pakistani madrasas raising security concerns. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Jakarta, Indonesia, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Indonesia. Indonesian experience with democracy, Islamic moderation and economic development interests Nigeria. Some Nigerian students study in Indonesian universities. Nigeria's Consulate General in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, is a critical consular mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Saudi Arabia's commercial capital. Nigeria's Consulate General in Johannesburg, South Africa, is one of Nigeria's most important consular missions representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in South Africa's economic capital. Located in Johannesburg, Africa's economic powerhouse and financial center, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs alongside Embassy in Pretoria. Johannesburg hosts large Nigerian diaspora including traders, students, professionals and families. However, Nigeria-South Africa relations are complicated by xenophobic attacks targeting Nigerian nationals, business rivalry between African giants, and competing continental leadership. The mission manages Nigeria's strategic relationship with UAE, major oil-producing nation and Middle East economic powerhouse. UAE is significant investor in Nigeria across oil and gas, aviation, real estate, and infrastructure sectors. Emirates Airlines operates extensive Nigerian routes. UAE hosts substantial Nigerian diaspora including businesspeople, students and professionals. The mission facilitates Nigeria's engagement with UAE sovereign wealth funds, coordinates on OPEC matters, and promotes investment attraction. Abu Dhabi hosts numerous international organizations and serves as diplomatic hub for Middle East region.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Accra, Ghana, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Ghana, one of Nigeria's most important bilateral relationships in West Africa. Located in Accra, Ghana's capital, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Nigeria-Ghana relations date to both countries' independence with deep historical, cultural and economic ties. Nigeria played crucial role supporting Ghana's independence and post-independence development. Both countries are ECOWAS founding members cooperating extensively on regional integration. However, relations have experienced tensions over treatment of Nigerian traders in Ghana, periodic expulsions, and business competition. The mission serves very large Nigerian diaspora including major trading community at Accra's markets. Both countries share borders through maritime boundaries in Gulf of Guinea.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Monrovia, Liberia, is one of Nigeria's most important diplomatic missions managing special relationship with West African neighbor. Located in Monrovia, Liberia's capital named after US President Monroe, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Juba, South Sudan, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in world's newest country (independent July 2011). Located in Juba, South Sudan's capital on White Nile, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission operates in one of world's most challenging environments characterized by active civil war, humanitarian catastrophe, state failure and extreme poverty despite vast oil reserves. South Sudan's independence from Sudan followed decades of civil war in which Nigeria supported mediation efforts. Nigeria has provided significant peacekeeping troops to UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) making the mission critical for coordinating peacekeeping operations. South Sudan descended into brutal civil war in 2013 between President Kiir and Vice President Machar factions, killing hundreds of thousands and displacing millions. Oil-rich but devastated by conflict, South Sudan faces famine, displacement and complete state collapse. Limited Nigerian community consists primarily of peacekeepers and few humanitarian workers. The mission operates under extraordinary security constraints requiring UN protection.

Investment and Securities Tribunal (IST) is specialized judicial tribunal adjudicating disputes in Nigeria's capital market and securities industry. Adjudicates disputes between investors and stockbrokers, companies and shareholders, and regulatory compliance issues. Tribunal comprises judges with securities law expertise. Conducts hearings, examines evidence and issues judgments enforceable like High Court orders. Appeals go to Court of Appeal. Provides specialized expertise in complex securities matters. Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (ISTH) Irrua is specialized federal tertiary hospital and teaching institution. Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) is federal examination body conducting entrance examinations and managing admissions into Nigerian tertiary institutions. Headquartered in Abuja with offices nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Established to standardize admission requirements and conduct common entrance examination (UTME - Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination) for universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. JAMB registers candidates for UTME annually with over 1.8 million candidates. Conducts computer-based UTME testing nationwide. Sets minimum admission requirements (cutoff marks) for tertiary institutions. Manages Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) where institutions admit students. Jos University Teaching Hospital (JUTH) is federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. Kainji National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and wildlife in northwestern Nigeria. Located across Niger, Kwara and Kebbi States covering approximately 5,341 square kilometers in two sectors (Borgu and Zugurma), operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established in 1979 following creation of Kainji Dam and Lake Kainji requiring wildlife conservation. The park protects savanna ecosystems, woodland and grassland habitats. Houses significant wildlife including elephants, hippopotamus, buffalo, various antelopes (roan, kob, hartebeest), lions, leopards, baboons and over 350 bird species. Borgu sector adjoins Benin's W National Park forming transboundary conservation complex. Faces threats from poaching, cattle grazing, illegal fishing in park waters and human encroachment. Tourism infrastructure limited but includes game viewing and safari camps. Park management involves anti-poaching patrols, habitat conservation, community engagement and sustainable tourism. Collaborates with Benin and Niger on transboundary wildlife conservation. Critical for northwestern Nigeria biodiversity protection and eco-tourism potential.

Kamuku National Park is federal protected area conserving biodiversity and ecosystems in northwestern Nigeria. King's College Lagos is prestigious federal government college and unity school. Located on Lagos Island, Lagos State, operating under Federal Ministry of Education. Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) is premier federal tertiary healthcare institution and teaching hospital. Legal Aid Council of Nigeria is federal agency providing free legal services to indigent citizens who cannot afford legal representation. mda_name: 563. LOWER BENUE RIVER BASIN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (LBRBDA)
mandate_description:
Lower Benue River Basin Development Authority (LBRBDA) is federal agency managing water resources, irrigation and agricultural development in Lower Benue River Basin. Headquartered in Makurdi covering Benue, Kogi, Nasarawa, Cross River, Ebonyi, Enugu and Anambra States, operating under Federal Ministry of Water Resources. Established as one of Nigeria's 12 River Basin Development Authorities. The basin includes Lower Benue River and tributaries. LBRBDA develops irrigation schemes supporting dry season farming. Constructs and operates small/medium dams for irrigation water supply. Manages water distribution to farmers and communities. Supports rice, vegetables and yam production through irrigation. Provides flood control infrastructure. Conducts hydrological studies and water resources assessment. Develops fadama (floodplain) irrigation exploiting seasonal water availability. Provides agricultural extension services to irrigated farmers. Faces challenges from flooding (Benue experiences major floods), inadequate infrastructure maintenance and farmer participation. Benue River's significant discharge creates both irrigation opportunities and flood risks requiring integrated management.

mda_name: 564. LOWER NIGER RIVER BASIN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (LNRBDA)

Maritime Academy of Nigeria Oron is premier federal maritime training institution providing education for seafarers and maritime professionals. Located in Oron, Akwa Ibom State in coastal south-south Nigeria, operating under Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) and Federal Ministry of Transportation. Offers certificate, diploma and degree programs in nautical science, marine engineering, maritime transport and related fields. Provides Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW) compliant training meeting International Maritime Organization (IMO) requirements. Trains deck officers (navigators), marine engineers, electro-technical officers and ratings. Operates training vessels for practical sea-going experience. Provides simulator training for navigation, engine room and ship handling. Offers specialized courses in ship security, survival at sea and marine operations. Trains for merchant navy careers. Collaborates with IMO, international maritime academies and shipping companies. Addresses shortage of qualified Nigerian seafarers in global shipping industry. Cabotage Act implementation increases demand for Nigerian seafarers. Faces challenges from inadequate vessels, equipment maintenance and international certification requirements.

mda_name: 566. MEDICAL AND DENTAL COUNCIL OF NIGERIA (MDCN)
mandate_description:
Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) is statutory regulatory body overseeing medical and dental professions. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under MDCN Act as independent regulatory authority. Established to regulate medical doctors, dentists and ensure professional standards protecting public health. Registers qualified medical practitioners and dentists. Accredits medical and dental schools ensuring quality training. Conducts professional examinations for foreign-trained doctors. Issues practicing licenses and annual practicing certificates. Enforces medical ethics and professional conduct. Investigates professional misconduct, medical negligence and quackery. Imposes disciplinary sanctions including suspension or deregistration. Monitors continuing medical education for practitioners. Regulates medical practice advertising and professional behavior. Collaborates with health facilities, medical associations (NMA, NDA) and international medical councils. Addresses challenges from quack doctors practicing illegally, medical brain drain and inadequate enforcement capacity. Maintains register of over 90,000 medical doctors and thousands of dentists. Critical for healthcare quality, patient safety and public trust in medical profession.

Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Board (MRTB) is statutory regulatory body overseeing physiotherapy, occupational therapy and other rehabilitation professions. mda_name: 570. MICHAEL IMODU INSTITUTE OF LABOUR STUDIES

Gashaka Gumti National Park is Nigeria's largest national park protecting biodiversity, wildlife and ecosystems. Located across Taraba and Adamawa States in northeastern Nigeria covering approximately 6,731 square kilometers, operating under Federal Ministry of Environment. Established in 1991 by merging Gashaka and Gumti Game Reserves creating Nigeria's premier wildlife conservation area. The park protects montane forests, savanna, grasslands and Nigeria's highest mountain peak (Chappal Waddi at 2,419 meters). Provides critical watershed for Taraba and Benue Rivers. Faces threats from poaching, illegal logging, cattle grazing encroachment and human-wildlife conflict. The basin includes Hadejia and Jama'are Rivers flowing into Lake Chad supporting extensive wetlands including Hadejia-Nguru wetlands. HJRBDA develops irrigation schemes, constructs dams, manages water distribution and supports dry season farming. Operates Tiga and Challawa Gorge Dams on Kano River providing irrigation water and flood control. Develops small and medium irrigation schemes for rice, wheat and vegetable production. Manages Hadejia-Nguru wetlands important for fishing, farming and biodiversity. Faces challenges from competing water uses, upstream dam impacts on downstream wetlands, climate variability and inadequate infrastructure maintenance. Supports rice production in Kano-Jigawa-Yobe irrigation schemes.

**Core Mandate:** To manage water resources, develop irrigation infrastructure, support agricultural production and protect wetlands in Hadejia-Jama'are river basin covering northern Nigeria states.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Manage water resources in Hadejia-Jama'are river basin across Kano, Jigawa, Yobe, Bauchi States
(b) Develop and operate irrigation schemes for dry season farming
(c) Construct, operate and maintain Tiga and Challawa Gorge Dams
(d) Distribute irrigation water to farmers and agricultural schemes
(e) Support rice, wheat and vegetable production through irrigation
(f) Develop small and medium irrigation infrastructure
(g) Manage Hadejia-Nguru wetlands conservation and sustainable use
(h) Provide flood control and water storage services
(i) Conduct hydrological monitoring and water resources assessment
(j) Allocate water among competing agricultural, domestic and environmental uses
(k) Support fisheries in reservoirs and wetlands
(l) Provide agricultural extension services to irrigated farmers
(m) Maintain irrigation canals, drains and water distribution infrastructure
(n) Conduct environmental impact assessments for water projects
(o) Engage communities in participatory water resources management
(p) Collaborate with State governments on irrigation development
(q) Address upstream-downstream water conflicts and wetland degradation
(r) Monitor water quality in rivers and reservoirs
(s) Adapt to climate variability affecting water availability
(t) Advance irrigation agriculture, water security and wetland conservation supporting rice production and livelihoods in northern Nigeria's critical agricultural basin

Health Records Registration Board is statutory regulatory body overseeing health records and health information management profession in Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Health. Established to regulate health information management practitioners ensuring professional standards in medical records, health information systems and data management across healthcare facilities. The Board registers qualified health records officers, accredits health information management training programs and enforces professional conduct standards. Ensures hospitals, clinics and health facilities maintain accurate, confidential patient medical records. Promotes electronic health records adoption and health information technology. Conducts professional examinations and issues practicing licenses. Investigates professional misconduct and enforces disciplinary measures. Collaborates with hospitals, health training institutions and international health information management associations. Addresses challenges from inadequate awareness, paper-based records predominance and limited electronic health records implementation. Critical for healthcare quality, patient safety, medical research and health data management.

**Core Mandate:** To regulate health records and health information management profession, ensure professional standards, promote quality medical records and advance health information systems in Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**

(b) Register qualified health records officers and health information managers
(c) Accredit health information management training programs in universities and polytechnics
(d) Conduct professional qualifying examinations for health records practitioners
(e) Issue practicing licenses to registered health information professionals
(f) Enforce professional conduct and ethical standards in medical records management
(g) Investigate complaints and professional misconduct by health records officers
(h) Impose disciplinary sanctions including suspension or deregistration for violations
(i) Promote accurate, complete and confidential patient medical records
(j) Advance electronic health records (EHR) adoption in healthcare facilities
(k) Develop standards for medical records documentation and management
(l) Promote health information technology and digital health systems
(m) Ensure compliance with medical records regulations across hospitals
(n) Provide continuing professional development for health information managers

(p) Promote patient data privacy and confidentiality standards
(q) Support health research through quality health data management

(s) Advocate for health information management profession development
(t) Advance healthcare quality, patient safety and evidence-based medicine through professional medical records management and modern health information systems

mda_name: 533. INDEPENDENT CORRUPT PRACTICES AND RELATED OFFENCES COMMISSION (ICPC)
mandate_description:
Independent Corrupt Practices and Related Offences Commission (ICPC) is federal anti-corruption agency investigating, preventing and prosecuting corruption in public sector. Headquartered in Abuja with zonal offices nationwide, operating as independent statutory body under ICPC Act 2000. Established to combat corruption complementing Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). ICPC focuses on corruption prevention, public sector corruption, abuse of office, gratification and system reforms strengthening integrity. Investigates corruption allegations against public officials including bribery, fraud, abuse of office and illicit enrichment. Prosecutes corruption cases in courts. Conducts Corruption Risk Assessments and System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities in MDAs. Promotes ethics, integrity and anti-corruption education. Monitors Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking implementation. Receives and investigates petitions from citizens. Operates independently though faces challenges from political interference, inadequate funding, lengthy prosecutions and weak conviction rates. Collaborates with EFCC, CCB, CCT and international anti-corruption agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To prevent, investigate and prosecute corruption in public sector; strengthen integrity systems; promote ethics; and advance anti-corruption reforms in Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Investigate corruption, bribery and abuse of office allegations in public sector
(b) Prosecute corrupt public officials in courts for corruption offenses
(c) Prevent corruption through system reforms and integrity strengthening
(d) Conduct Corruption Risk Assessments in Ministries, Departments and Agencies
(e) Perform System Study Reviews identifying corruption vulnerabilities
(f) Monitor Constituency Projects and capital releases tracking fund utilization
(g) Receive, investigate and act on corruption petitions from citizens
(h) Investigate gratification, bribery and illicit enrichment by public officials
(i) Prosecute abuse of office, fraud and corruption in procurement
(j) Promote ethics, integrity and anti-corruption values in public service
(k) Conduct anti-corruption education in schools, MDAs and communities
(l) Enforce asset declaration requirements for public officials
(m) Collaborate with EFCC on joint anti-corruption operations
(n) Coordinate with Code of Conduct Bureau on asset verification
(o) Provide technical assistance to MDAs on corruption prevention
(p) Conduct public enlightenment campaigns on corruption reporting
(q) Collaborate with civil society organizations on anti-corruption advocacy
(r) Coordinate with international anti-corruption agencies and conventions
(s) Recommend policy and legislative reforms strengthening anti-corruption frameworks
(t) Advance Nigeria's anti-corruption fight through prevention, investigation, prosecution and systemic reforms reducing corruption in public institutions

Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is Nigeria's electoral management body conducting elections, voter registration and electoral processes. Headquartered in Abuja with offices in all 36 states and 774 Local Governments, operating as constitutionally established independent commission. Mandated by 1999 Constitution and Electoral Act to organize, conduct and supervise elections for President, National Assembly, Governors and State Assemblies. INEC registers voters through Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) maintaining national voter register. Conducts elections including presidential, gubernatorial, National Assembly, State Assembly and Area Council elections. Registers political parties and monitors party activities. Delimits constituencies for electoral purposes. Conducts voter education promoting electoral participation. Procures electoral materials including ballot papers, result sheets and Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) technology. Recruits and trains ad hoc election staff. Announces election results and issues Certificates of Return to winners. Faces challenges from electoral violence, logistical difficulties, result manipulation allegations, voter apathy and political interference despite constitutional independence.

**Core Mandate:** To organize, conduct and supervise free, fair and credible elections; register voters and political parties; promote electoral participation; and strengthen Nigeria's democracy through professional electoral management.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Organize, conduct and supervise presidential elections every four years
(b) Conduct National Assembly elections for Senate and House of Representatives
(c) Organize gubernatorial elections in 36 states
(d) Conduct State Houses of Assembly elections across Nigeria
(e) Organize Area Council elections in Federal Capital Territory
(f) Register eligible Nigerian citizens as voters through Continuous Voter Registration
(g) Maintain and update National Register of Voters
(h) Register political parties meeting constitutional requirements
(i) Monitor political party activities and campaign finances
(j) Delimit constituencies for National Assembly and State Assemblies
(k) Conduct voter education and public enlightenment on electoral processes
(l) Procure electoral materials including ballot papers and result sheets
(m) Deploy Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for voter authentication
(n) Recruit, train and deploy ad hoc election staff including Presiding Officers
(o) Collate and announce election results at ward, LGA, state and national levels
(p) Issue Certificates of Return to elected officials
(q) Address electoral offenses including vote buying and ballot stuffing
(r) Conduct bye-elections and re-run elections as ordered by courts
(s) Collaborate with security agencies on election security
(t) Advance Nigeria's democracy through credible electoral processes, transparent result management and continuous electoral reforms strengthening public confidence in democratic governance

Industrial Arbitration Panel (IAP) is specialized tribunal adjudicating industrial disputes between employers and workers in Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment per Trade Disputes Act. Established to resolve industrial disputes through arbitration avoiding prolonged strikes disrupting economy. IAP hears trade disputes referred by Minister of Labour when conciliation fails. Adjudicates disputes on wages, conditions of employment, termination, unfair labor practices and collective bargaining disagreements. Panel comprises neutral arbitrators with labor law expertise. Conducts hearings, examines evidence, hears parties and issues binding awards. Awards are enforceable in National Industrial Court. Provides faster dispute resolution than courts. Addresses disputes in critical sectors including oil/gas, banking, aviation, health and education. Promotes industrial harmony and peaceful labor relations. Faces challenges from parties' non-compliance with awards, legal challenges to jurisdiction and limited enforcement mechanisms. Complements National Industrial Court and labor ministry conciliation services.

**Core Mandate:** To adjudicate industrial disputes through arbitration, issue binding awards, promote industrial harmony and resolve employer-worker conflicts in Nigerian labor market.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Adjudicate industrial disputes referred by Minister of Labour and Employment
(b) Hear trade disputes between employers and workers/unions
(c) Arbitrate disputes on wages, salaries and remuneration
(d) Resolve conflicts over conditions of employment and workplace rights
(e) Adjudicate wrongful termination and unfair dismissal disputes
(f) Address unfair labor practices by employers or unions
(g) Resolve collective bargaining disagreements
(h) Conduct arbitration hearings in industrial dispute cases
(i) Examine evidence, witness testimonies and parties' submissions
(j) Issue binding arbitration awards resolving disputes
(k) Enforce awards through National Industrial Court mechanisms
(l) Prevent or end strikes through binding dispute resolution
(m) Promote industrial peace and harmonious labor relations
(n) Address disputes in critical sectors (oil/gas, banking, aviation, health)
(o) Provide expedited alternative to lengthy court litigation
(p) Protect workers' rights while balancing employers' interests
(q) Interpret collective agreements and employment contracts
(r) Coordinate with Ministry of Labour on labor dispute management
(s) Collaborate with National Industrial Court on enforcement
(t) Advance industrial harmony, prevent disruptive strikes and resolve employer-worker conflicts protecting Nigeria's economic stability and workers' rights

Industrial Training Fund (ITF) is premier federal skills development agency providing vocational training, skills acquisition and human capital development for Nigerian workforce. Headquartered in Jos, Plateau State with Area Offices and Model Skills Training Centres nationwide, operating under Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment. Established by ITF Act 2011 to promote acquisition of skills in industry and commerce. ITF collects 1% levy from companies with 5+ employees (payroll ≥N50 million annually) financing training programs. Provides skills training in technical trades, industrial skills, entrepreneurship and modern technologies. Operates Model Skills Training Centres offering courses in welding, electrical, automotive, construction, ICT and other trades. Reimburses companies' training costs through levy rebate system. Conducts National Industrial Skills Development Programme (NISDP). Offers entrepreneurship training for unemployed youth. Provides Train-the-Trainer programs for instructors. Conducts apprenticeship programs linking trainees with employers. Addresses youth unemployment, skills mismatch and inadequate technical workforce. Collaborates with industries, training institutions and international skills development agencies.

**Core Mandate:** To promote skills acquisition, provide vocational training, develop industrial workforce, support entrepreneurship and reduce unemployment through comprehensive skills development programs.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Promote acquisition of industrial, technical and vocational skills across sectors
(b) Collect 1% training levy from companies with 5+ employees for training funding
(c) Administer levy rebate scheme reimbursing companies' approved training costs
(d) Operate Model Skills Training Centres providing practical vocational training
(e) Conduct National Industrial Skills Development Programme (NISDP)
(f) Provide skills training in welding, fabrication, electrical and mechanical trades
(g) Offer automotive mechanics, building construction and plumbing training

(s) Coordinate with TVETIs, polytechnics and technical colleges

Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) is federal regulatory agency overseeing Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and infrastructure concessions in Nigeria. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission Act 2005 under Presidency. Established to regulate PPP projects ensuring value for money, fiscal sustainability and public interest protection. ICRC provides technical support to MDAs developing PPP projects. Conducts Outline Business Case (OBC) and Full Business Case (FBC) reviews approving projects. Issues Compliance Certificates for PPP projects meeting regulatory requirements. Monitors concession agreements implementation. Maintains PPP project database. Provides capacity building for MDAs on PPP procurement. Develops guidelines, regulations and standard templates for PPP contracts. Conducts Value for Money assessments ensuring taxpayers benefit from PPPs. Reviews unsolicited proposals from private sector. Addresses fiscal risks from government guarantees in PPPs. Promotes transparent, competitive PPP procurement. Has reviewed major projects including Lekki-Epe Expressway, Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 2 and others. Faces challenges from limited PPP financing, capacity gaps and slow project approvals.

**Core Mandate:** To regulate Public-Private Partnerships, ensure value for money, provide technical PPP support to MDAs, monitor concessions and promote sustainable infrastructure delivery through private sector participation.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Regulate Public-Private Partnership (PPP) projects across federal MDAs
(b) Review and approve Outline Business Cases (OBC) for PPP projects
(c) Review and approve Full Business Cases (FBC) before PPP procurement
(d) Issue Compliance Certificates to PPP projects meeting regulatory requirements
(e) Monitor implementation of concession agreements and PPP contracts
(f) Provide technical support to MDAs developing PPP projects
(g) Conduct Value for Money (VfM) assessments ensuring public benefits
(h) Review unsolicited proposals from private sector investors
(9) Develop PPP regulations, guidelines and policy frameworks

mda_name: 538. INSTITUTE FOR PEACE AND CONFLICT RESOLUTION (IPCR)
mandate_description:
Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR) is federal agency promoting peace, preventing conflicts and mediating disputes across Nigeria. Located in Abuja, operating under Office of Secretary to Government of the Federation. Established in 2000 to address Nigeria's numerous conflicts including ethnic, religious, communal, land and political disputes. IPCR conducts conflict early warning monitoring potential flashpoints. Provides mediation and dialogue facilitation in communal conflicts. Conducts peace education and training on conflict resolution. Develops National Policy on Peacebuilding and Conflict Management. Operates Peace and Conflict Review magazine. Trains security personnel, traditional rulers, religious leaders and youth in conflict prevention. Conducts research on conflict drivers and peace interventions. Mediates farmer-herder conflicts, communal clashes, electoral violence and boundary disputes. Collaborates with ECOWAS Early Warning System. Provides conflict assessments for government interventions. Organizes peace summits and dialogue forums. Faces challenges from proliferation of conflicts, limited resources, enforcement gaps and political interference in conflict mediation.

**Core Mandate:** To promote peace, prevent conflicts, provide mediation services, conduct peace education and support government conflict resolution efforts across Nigeria.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Promote peace, stability and conflict prevention across Nigeria
(b) Conduct conflict early warning monitoring potential crisis areas
(c) Provide mediation and dialogue facilitation in communal conflicts
(d) Conduct peace education and conflict resolution training
(e) Train security personnel on conflict-sensitive approaches
(f) Provide peace and conflict training for traditional and religious leaders
(g) Conduct conflict resolution training for youth and civil society
(h) Develop National Policy on Peacebuilding and Conflict Management
(i) Conduct research on conflict drivers, dynamics and peace interventions
(j) Mediate farmer-herder conflicts destroying livelihoods

mda_name: 539. INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND TRAINING (IAR&T), IBADAN
mandate_description:
Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T) Ibadan is federal agricultural research institution conducting research on tropical agriculture, crop production and agricultural technologies. Located at Moor Plantation, Ibadan, Oyo State, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established in 1969 focusing on southwestern Nigeria agroecological zone. IAR&T conducts research on major crops including cassava, maize, yam, cocoa, oil palm, plantain, vegetables and tree crops. Develops improved crop varieties with higher yields, disease resistance and climate adaptation. Researches soil fertility management, integrated pest management and sustainable farming systems. Conducts agroforestry and soil conservation research. Develops agricultural technologies and farming practices. Trains farmers, extension agents and agricultural students. Multiplies and distributes improved seeds and planting materials. Operates demonstration farms showcasing research results. Publishes research findings and technical bulletins. Collaborates with IITA, universities and international agricultural research centers. Addresses food security, climate change adaptation and sustainable agriculture in southwestern Nigeria and beyond.

**Core Mandate:** To conduct agricultural research, develop improved crop varieties, generate agricultural technologies and provide training supporting food security and agricultural development in Nigeria.

(t) Advance food security, agricultural productivity and sustainable farming in southwestern Nigeria and nationally through scientific research and technology generation

Institute for Agricultural Research (IAR) Zaria is premier federal agricultural research institution conducting research on crops, livestock and agricultural systems in northern Nigeria. Located at Ahmadu Bello University, Samaru, Zaria, Kaduna State, operating under Agricultural Research Council of Nigeria and Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established in 1922 (originally as research station), IAR is Nigeria's oldest agricultural research institute. Focuses on savanna agroecology covering northern Nigeria. Conducts research on sorghum, millet, groundnut, cowpea, rice, cotton, sesame and other dryland crops. Develops drought-tolerant crop varieties for semi-arid regions. Researches livestock production including cattle, small ruminants and poultry. Conducts integrated crop-livestock systems research. Develops farming systems for sustainable Sahel agriculture. Researches soil and water conservation for semi-arid environments. Provides technical advice on agricultural policies. Trains farmers, extension workers and students. Multiplies and distributes seeds of improved varieties. Collaborates with ICRISAT, IITA and international dryland agriculture research centers. Addresses food security, drought resilience and poverty in northern Nigeria's agricultural economy.

**Core Mandate:** To conduct agricultural research for savanna agroecology, develop drought-tolerant crop varieties, research livestock systems and support northern Nigeria's agricultural development and food security.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Tunis, Tunisia, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Tunisian Republic. Located in Tunis, Tunisia's capital on Mediterranean coast and birthplace of Arab Spring uprisings, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's relationship with North African moderate democracy. Tunisia's 2011 Jasmine Revolution sparked Arab Spring across Middle East and North Africa. Limited Nigerian community includes students attracted by Arab-African culture, traders and migrants using Tunisia as transit point attempting Mediterranean crossing to Europe. Tunisia maintained democracy better than other Arab Spring countries but faces severe economic challenges, youth unemployment and political instability. Nigerian migrants detained in Tunisia while attempting European entry. Both countries cooperate in African Union. Tunisia has agricultural expertise particularly olive production and tourism experience. Historic Carthage heritage provides cultural richness. The mission addresses irregular migration transit issues, promotes bilateral trade, coordinates AU engagement, protects limited diaspora and maintains North African presence while supporting Tunisia's fragile democratic experiment.

**Core Mandate:** To represent Nigeria's interests in Tunisia, manage migration transit issues, promote bilateral trade, support democratic transition, protect diaspora and maintain North African diplomatic presence.

(s) Promote Nigeria's positive image in North Africa and Arab world
(t) Advance Nigeria's interests in North African engagement, migration management and African Union cooperation

Nigeria's Foreign Mission to Vatican City (Holy See) is a specialized diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria to Vatican City State and global Catholic Church. Located in Vatican City, world's smallest sovereign state within Rome, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages Nigeria's religious diplomatic relationship with Catholic Church headquarters and Pope. Nigeria has Africa's largest Catholic population with approximately 30 million Catholics representing about 15% of Nigerian population concentrated in southern regions. Vatican exercises significant influence over Nigerian Catholics and provides humanitarian assistance to Nigeria. Nigerian Cardinals including Francis Arinze participate in Papal elections and Vatican leadership. Vatican addresses Nigerian religious conflicts, Boko Haram persecution of Christians and promotes inter-religious dialogue between Nigerian Christians and Muslims. Pope Francis has condemned Boko Haram attacks on Nigerian Christians. Vatican City hosts Nigerian Catholic pilgrims visiting St. Peter's Basilica. The mission coordinates religious diplomacy, addresses Christian persecution in northern Nigeria, facilitates Vatican humanitarian assistance, protects Nigerian pilgrims and represents Nigerian Catholic interests to global Church leadership.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Vienna, Austria, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Austria with accreditation to international organizations headquartered in Vienna. Located in Vienna, Austria's capital on Danube River hosting major UN agencies and international organizations, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages limited Nigeria-Austria bilateral relations but holds strategic importance for international organization engagement. Vienna hosts UN Office (UNOV), International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) headquarters, Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and numerous other international bodies. Limited Nigerian diaspora includes students and professionals. Austria is wealthy EU member with strong economy and culture. Nigeria engages IAEA on peaceful nuclear energy development for electricity generation addressing power shortages. OPEC headquarters location makes Vienna absolutely critical for coordinating oil production policies and prices. The mission coordinates OPEC ministerial meetings, participates in IAEA nuclear cooperation programs, engages UN agencies, protects limited diaspora and maintains crucial presence in international organization hub city.

Nigeria's Foreign Mission in Warsaw, Poland, is a diplomatic mission representing Federal Republic of Nigeria in Republic of Poland. Located in Warsaw, Poland's capital rebuilt after WWII devastation, operating under Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The mission manages limited bilateral engagement with Central European EU member experiencing rapid economic growth. Growing Nigerian community includes students attracted by affordable EU education quality and migrants. Poland played crucial unexpected role during Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, serving as primary evacuation route for thousands of Nigerian students fleeing Ukraine through Polish border crossings. Polish authorities and citizens provided humanitarian assistance to evacuating Nigerian students. Some Nigerian irregular migrants transit Poland attempting Western European entry. Poland's economic transformation from communism to emerging EU economy creates opportunities. However, Poland has conservative Law and Justice government and some anti-immigrant sentiment in society. Limited Polish investment in Nigeria. The mission protects growing diaspora, coordinates Ukraine border crossing support during evacuations, promotes educational cooperation, facilitates minimal trade and maintains Central European diplomatic presence despite limited bilateral engagement.

**Core Mandate:** To represent Nigeria's interests in Poland, protect diaspora, coordinate Ukraine border evacuation support, promote educational ties and maintain Central European diplomatic presence.

**Statutory Functions:**

(i) Provide guarantees facilitating commercial bank agricultural lending
(j) Finance agricultural research and development initiatives
(k) Support climate-smart agriculture and sustainable farming practices
(l) Finance livestock development and animal production projects
(m) Support fisheries and aquaculture development
(n) Finance post-harvest infrastructure including storage and processing
(o) Provide working capital for agricultural input suppliers
(p) Support agricultural export development and value addition
(q) Collaborate with CBN on Anchor Borrowers Program
(r) Coordinate with Bank of Agriculture on agricultural financing
(s) Monitor loan utilization and ensure credit recovery
(t) Advance agricultural productivity and commercialization through accessible financing reducing capital constraints for farmers and agribusinesses

National Agricultural Insurance Corporation is federal agency providing crop insurance and agricultural risk management. Headquartered in Abuja, operating under Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established to protect farmers against crop losses from natural disasters, pests, diseases and climate variability. Operates Nigeria Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) providing subsidized crop insurance. Insures crops against drought, flood, pests, diseases and other perils. Provides livestock insurance for cattle, poultry and fish farms. Insures agricultural assets including equipment and infrastructure. Offers index-based insurance using weather parameters. Provides forest insurance for tree plantations. Conducts damage assessment and pays compensation to insured farmers. Government provides premium subsidy making insurance affordable. Promotes agricultural insurance awareness among farming communities. Collaborates with state governments, insurance companies and farmers' organizations. Addresses challenges from low insurance penetration (less than 1% farmers insured), delayed claims payment, limited awareness and adverse selection. Critical for risk management, encouraging agricultural investment and protecting farmers' livelihoods from climate shocks.

**Core Mandate:** To provide agricultural insurance, protect farmers against crop losses, manage agricultural risks and promote insurance adoption supporting farming resilience and food security.

**Statutory Functions:**

(b) Provide crop insurance protecting against natural disasters and pests
(c) Insure crops against drought, flood, hailstorm and fire

(e) Offer livestock insurance for cattle, goats, sheep and pigs
(f) Provide poultry insurance for commercial chicken production
(g) Insure fish farms and aquaculture projects
(h) Provide insurance for agricultural equipment and machinery
(i) Offer infrastructure insurance for storage facilities and processing plants
(j) Develop index-based insurance using rainfall and weather data
(k) Provide forest insurance for timber plantations
(l) Conduct damage assessment and loss verification
(m) Pay compensation to insured farmers suffering losses
(n) Administer government premium subsidy program (50-80% subsidy)
(o) Promote agricultural insurance awareness among farmers
(p) Train insurance agents on agricultural insurance products
(q) Collaborate with state governments on farmer registration
(r) Partner with insurance companies on underwriting
(s) Develop innovative insurance products for smallholder farmers
(t) Advance agricultural risk management and farmer protection increasing insurance penetration supporting climate resilience and encouraging agricultural investment

National Agricultural Land Development Authority is federal agency developing agricultural lands, irrigation and farm infrastructure. Operating under Office of President (previously Federal Ministry of Agriculture). Re-established/revitalized in 2020 to promote large-scale farming and address food security. Develops and reclaims agricultural lands for cultivation. Establishes integrated farms demonstrating modern agriculture. Develops irrigation infrastructure for all-season farming. Promotes mechanized agriculture and large-scale farming. Establishes Young Farmers Scheme training youth in agriculture. Provides agricultural inputs and extension services. Develops commodity value chains including rice, cassava, aquaculture and livestock. Establishes processing facilities for agricultural products. Coordinates with CBN Anchor Borrowers Program. Addresses food security and agricultural unemployment. Collaborates with state governments establishing farm estates. Faces challenges from land acquisition, funding and sustainability of established farms. Represents government direct intervention in agricultural production beyond traditional extension approach.

**Core Mandate:** To develop agricultural lands, establish integrated farms, promote mechanized agriculture, train young farmers and directly boost food production through government-led farming initiatives.

**Statutory Functions:**
(a) Develop and reclaim agricultural lands for cultivation
(b) Establish integrated farms across states demonstrating modern agriculture
(c) Develop irrigation infrastructure enabling dry season farming
(d) Promote mechanized agriculture using tractors and modern equipment
(e) Establish large-scale commodity farms for rice, maize and other crops
(f) Operate Young Farmers Scheme training youth in agriculture
(g) Provide agricultural inputs including seeds, fertilizers and chemicals
(h) Offer agricultural extension services and technical support
(i) Develop rice value chain including production, processing and marketing
(j) Promote cassava production and processing for industrial use
(k) Establish aquaculture farms for fish production
(l) Develop livestock farms for poultry, cattle and small ruminants
(m) Establish processing facilities for agricultural products
(n) Create farm estates and agricultural settlements
(o) Coordinate with CBN Anchor Borrowers Program on input supply
(p) Address youth unemployment through agricultural training and employment
(q) Promote food security through increased domestic production
(r) Collaborate with state governments on land allocation
(s) Establish demonstration farms showcasing best practices
(t) Advance food production and agricultural transformation through direct government farming initiatives, mechanization and youth engagement reducing food imports

National Agriculture Seeds Council is federal regulatory agency overseeing seed industry, variety release and seed certification. Operating under Federal Ministry of Agriculture. Established to regulate seed production, distribution and ensure quality seeds for farmers. Registers and releases new crop varieties for commercial production. Conducts variety evaluation trials assessing performance. Certifies seeds ensuring genetic purity and quality. Licenses seed companies and producers. Regulates seed importation and exportation. Maintains National Crop Varieties and Livestock Breeds Register. Enforces seed quality standards and labeling requirements. Conducts seed testing in laboratories. Promotes use of improved and certified seeds. Protects plant breeders' rights. Coordinates with agricultural research institutes on variety release. Addresses challenges from fake seeds, weak enforcement and limited seed production capacity. Quality seeds critical for agricultural productivity improvements - seed quality determines 30-40% of crop yields. Ensures farmers access genetically pure, disease-free and high-yielding seeds.

**Core Mandate:** To regulate seed industry, certify quality seeds, release improved varieties, license seed producers and ensure farmers access to high-quality planting materials.
